## Roadmap

```{r process-flow, fig.width=6.6, fig.height=3.15, fig.align="center"}
crukdark <- "#00007E"

## everything the roadmap needs lives in its own environment, so later
## chunks that reuse names such as r or cx cannot change the drawing
draw_roadmap <- local({
  circle <- function(cx, cy, r, n = 200) {
    th <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n)
    list(x = cx + r * cos(th), y = cy + r * sin(th))
  }


  stages <- c("Stage 1", "Stage 2", "Stage 3", "Stage 4")
  capt   <- list(c("Problem", "Statement", ""),
                 list("FWER Control", expression("via Raw " * italic(p) * "-value"), "Adjustment"),
                 c("FWER Control via the", "Joint Distribution of", "Test Statistics"),
                 c("FDR Control", "and Estimation", ""))
  prefix <- c(NA, "FWER", "FWER", "FDR")
  fills  <- c("#FF0087", "#009CEE", "#00007E", "#FF0087")
  cx     <- c(1, 3.00, 5.00, 7.00)
  r      <- 0.56

  draw_line <- function(x, y, txt, cex, bold_prefix = NA,
                        col = "grey15", col_prefix = "black") {
    if (is.na(bold_prefix) || identical(txt, "")) {
      text(x, y, txt, cex = cex, col = col)
      return(invisible())
    }
    rest  <- sub(paste0("^", bold_prefix), "", txt)
    w1    <- strwidth(bold_prefix, cex = cex, font = 2)
    w2    <- strwidth(rest, cex = cex, font = 1)
    x0    <- x - (w1 + w2) / 2
    text(x0, y, bold_prefix, cex = cex, col = col_prefix, font = 2, adj = c(0, 0.5))
    text(x0 + w1, y, rest, cex = cex, col = col, adj = c(0, 0.5))
  }

  ## highlight = NA draws every stage in colour; a stage number greys out the others
  function(highlight = NA) {
    par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
    plot(NULL, xlim = c(0.30, 7.70), ylim = c(-1.62, 0.8), asp = 1,
         axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")

    for (i in seq_along(cx)) {
      on  <- is.na(highlight) || i == highlight
      col <- if (on) "grey15" else "grey72"
      if (i < length(cx)) {
        arrows(cx[i] + r + 0.06, 0, cx[i + 1] - r - 0.06, 0,
               length = 0.13, lwd = 2.4, col = "grey55")
      }
      polygon(circle(cx[i], 0, r), col = if (on) fills[i] else "grey85", border = NA)
      text(cx[i], 0, stages[i], col = "white", cex = 1.18, font = 2)
      draw_line(cx[i], -(r + 0.19), capt[[i]][[1]], cex = 0.68, bold_prefix = prefix[i],
                col = col, col_prefix = if (on) "black" else "grey72")
      draw_line(cx[i], -(r + 0.37), capt[[i]][[2]], cex = 0.68, col = col)
      draw_line(cx[i], -(r + 0.55), capt[[i]][[3]], cex = 0.68, col = col)
    }
  }
})

draw_roadmap()
```

\vspace{-0.3em}

\noindent\hspace*{0.051\linewidth}\footnotesize\textbf{FWER}: Family-Wise Error Rate \newline \hspace*{0.051\linewidth}\textbf{FDR}: False Discovery Rate\normalsize

## Statistical concepts used for data-driven decisions {.t}

```{r population-model, include=FALSE}

pdf("population-distribution.pdf", width = 4.6, height = 3.0)
par(mar = c(2.6, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5), mgp = c(1.5, 0.45, 0))

dfree <- 3
xlim  <- c(0, 15)

xs <- seq(xlim[1], xlim[2], length.out = 1200)
ys <- dchisq(xs, dfree)

plot(NULL, xlim = xlim, ylim = c(0, max(ys) * 1.18),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
lines(xs, ys, col = crukdark, lwd = 2)
axis(1, at = seq(0, 15, 3), cex.axis = 1.02, lwd = 1.1)
dev.off()
```

## A hypothesis about $\mu$ {.t}

```{r population-bp, include=FALSE}
crukdark <- "#00007E"

pdf("population-bp.pdf", width = 4.6, height = 3.0)
par(mar = c(2.6, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5), mgp = c(1.5, 0.45, 0))

mu <- 110; sdev <- 15
xlim <- c(mu - 3.4 * sdev, mu + 3.4 * sdev)

xs <- seq(xlim[1], xlim[2], length.out = 1200)
ys <- dnorm(xs, mu, sdev)

plot(NULL, xlim = xlim, ylim = c(0, max(ys) * 1.28),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
lines(xs, ys, col = crukdark, lwd = 2)

## mu: dashed vertical line through the peak
segments(mu, 0, mu, dnorm(mu, mu, sdev), col = crukdark, lty = 2, lwd = 1.6)
text(mu, dnorm(mu, mu, sdev), expression(mu), pos = 3, offset = 0.3,
     col = crukdark, cex = 2.2)

## sigma: from mu to mu + sigma, at the height of the inflection point
y_s <- dnorm(mu + sdev, mu, sdev)
arrows(mu, y_s, mu + sdev, y_s, code = 3, length = 0.08, angle = 25,
       col = crukdark, lwd = 1.8)
text(mu + sdev / 2, y_s, expression(sigma), pos = 3, offset = 0.3,
     col = crukdark, cex = 2.1)

axis(1, at = seq(70, 150, 20), cex.axis = 1.02, lwd = 1.1)
mtext("Systolic blood pressure (mmHg)", side = 1, line = 1.5, cex = 0.92)
dev.off()
```

## Null hypothesis ($H_0$) and statistical errors {.t}

\vspace{0em}

\begingroup
\setlength{\leftmargini}{0pt}

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ We can never prove that a hypothesis ($H_0$) is \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE}

\hangindent=9pt\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ We can \textbf{reject} $H_0$ (declare it \colorbox{green}{\color{black}FALSE}), accepting a \textbf{controlled probability} $\alpha$ of rejecting it when it is actually \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE}

\endgroup

\vspace{-0.4em}

\begin{center}
\large\textbf{Hence, we want to control the probability of false positive statements\\ (i.e.~avoiding false statements about the population)}
\end{center}

\begin{tikzpicture}[remember picture, overlay]
\node[anchor=center, inner sep=0] at ([yshift=-167.25pt]current page.north) {\fontsize{13}{16}\selectfont\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}%
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\hline
$H_0$ & Not Rejected & Rejected \\
\hline
\colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE}  & \color{crukdark}$1 - \alpha$ & \colorbox{crukpink}{\color{crukdark}$\alpha$} \\
\colorbox{green}{\color{black}FALSE} & \color{crukdark}$\beta$ & \color{crukdark}$1 - \beta$ \\
\hline
\end{tabular}};
\node[anchor=south west, inner sep=0, align=left, font=\normalsize] at ([xshift=10.5pt,yshift=20pt]current page.south west) {%
\colorbox{crukpink}{\color{crukdark}$\alpha$} $= \mathrm{P}(\text{reject } H_0 \mid H_0 \text{ TRUE})$: \textbf{Type I error rate} (false positive, significance level)\\[2pt]
$\textcolor{crukdark}{\beta} = \mathrm{P}(\text{fail to reject } H_0 \mid H_0 \text{ FALSE})$: \textbf{Type II error rate} (false negative)\\[2pt]
$\textcolor{crukdark}{1 - \beta} = \mathrm{P}(\text{reject } H_0 \mid H_0 \text{ FALSE})$: \textbf{Statistical power} (true positive)};
\end{tikzpicture}

## Hypothesis tests as decision functions

```{r chisq-generic, include=FALSE}
crukdark  <- "#00007E"
cruklight <- "#009CEE"
crukpink  <- "#FF0087"

pdf("chisq-distribution.pdf", width = 4.6, height = 3.0)
par(mar = c(3.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5), mgp = c(1.5, 0.45, 0))

dfree <- 9
ccrit <- qchisq(0.95, dfree)   # 16.92
cobs  <- 19.5                  # a generic observed statistic, p = 0.021
xlim  <- c(0, 30)

xs <- seq(xlim[1], xlim[2], length.out = 1200)
ys <- dchisq(xs, dfree)

plot(NULL, xlim = xlim, ylim = c(0, max(ys) * 1.18),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")

## the 5% rejection region in the upper tail
xr <- seq(ccrit, xlim[2], length.out = 400)
polygon(c(xr, rev(xr)), c(dchisq(xr, dfree), rep(0, length(xr))),
        col = crukpink, border = NA)

## the p-value: the area beyond the observed statistic, hatched over the
## critical region so that it is visibly a SUBSET of the 5% (p = 0.021 < 0.05)
xp <- seq(cobs, xlim[2], length.out = 400)
polygon(c(xp, rev(xp)), c(dchisq(xp, dfree), rep(0, length(xp))),
        col = cruklight, border = NA, density = 32, angle = 45, lwd = 1.6)
segments(cobs, 0, cobs, dchisq(cobs, dfree), col = cruklight, lwd = 1.3)

lines(xs, ys, col = crukdark, lwd = 2)

axis(1, at = seq(0, 30, 5), cex.axis = 1.02, lwd = 1.1)
mtext(expression(chi^2), side = 1, line = 2.05, cex = 1.2)

segments(ccrit, 0, ccrit, dchisq(ccrit, dfree), col = crukpink, lwd = 1.4)
text(ccrit - 0.3, 0.034, "5%", col = crukpink,
     cex = 0.96, adj = c(1, 0.5))

## pink "Critical region" box, sized to its text
lab <- "Critical region"
lcex <- 0.98
bx <- 17.5; by <- max(ys) * 0.78
bw <- strwidth(lab, cex = lcex) * 1.22
bh <- strheight(lab, cex = lcex) * 1.5
rect(bx - bw/2, by - bh, bx + bw/2, by + bh,
     border = crukpink, lwd = 1.4, col = "white")
text(bx, by, lab, col = crukpink, cex = lcex, font = 2)
arrows(bx - bw/2 * 0.35, by - bh, ccrit + 0.8, 0.008, length = 0.05,
       lwd = 1.2, col = crukpink)

## light-blue "p-value" box, pointing at the area beyond t_s
lab <- expression(bolditalic(p) * bold("-value"))
bx <- 25.5; by <- max(ys) * 0.42
bw <- strwidth(lab, cex = lcex) * 1.35
bh <- strheight(lab, cex = lcex) * 1.5
rect(bx - bw/2, by - bh, bx + bw/2, by + bh,
     border = cruklight, lwd = 1.4, col = "white")
text(bx, by, lab, col = cruklight, cex = lcex, font = 2)
arrows(bx - bw/2 * 0.3, by - bh, cobs + 1.6, 0.003, length = 0.05,
       lwd = 1.2, col = cruklight)

## the observed statistic, sitting on the axis
points(cobs, 0, pch = 19, col = cruklight, cex = 1.9)
text(cobs, 0.013, expression(italic(t)[s]), col = cruklight,
     cex = 1.14, font = 2, adj = c(0.5, 0))

text(15, max(ys) * 1.13,
     expression(chi^2 ~ "distribution," ~ df == 9),
     col = crukdark, cex = 1.03)
dev.off()
```

\end{minipage} \\

## Student's $t$-test

```{r tdist-onesample, include=FALSE}
crukdark  <- "#00007E"
cruklight <- "#009CEE"
crukpink  <- "#FF0087"

pdf("t-distribution.pdf", width = 4.6, height = 3.0)
par(mar = c(2.6, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5), mgp = c(1.5, 0.45, 0))

dfree <- 5
tcrit <- qt(0.975, dfree)
tobs  <- 9.185387
## symmetric window, so that BOTH tails of the two-sided test are visible
xlim  <- c(-8.8, 8.8)

xs <- seq(xlim[1], xlim[2], length.out = 1200)
ys <- dt(xs, dfree)
ymax <- max(ys)

plot(NULL, xlim = xlim, ylim = c(0, ymax * 1.46),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")

## the two 2.5% rejection regions
for (sgn in c(-1, 1)) {
  xx <- if (sgn < 0) seq(xlim[1], -tcrit, length.out = 400) else seq(tcrit, xlim[2], length.out = 400)
  polygon(c(xx, rev(xx)), c(dt(xx, dfree), rep(0, length(xx))),
          col = crukpink, border = NA)
}

## the two-sided p-value: both areas beyond |t_s|, hatched on top of the
## critical region so that it is visibly a SUBSET of the 5%
for (sgn in c(-1, 1)) {
  xx <- if (sgn < 0) seq(xlim[1], -tobs, length.out = 300) else seq(tobs, xlim[2], length.out = 300)
  polygon(c(xx, rev(xx)), c(dt(xx, dfree), rep(0, length(xx))),
          col = cruklight, border = cruklight, density = 40, angle = 45, lwd = 1.5)
}

lines(xs, ys, col = crukdark, lwd = 2)

axis(1, at = seq(-8, 8, 4), cex.axis = 1.02, lwd = 1.1)
mtext(expression(italic(t)), side = 1, line = 1.5, cex = 1.2)

segments(-tcrit, 0, -tcrit, dt(-tcrit, dfree), col = crukpink, lwd = 1.4)
segments( tcrit, 0,  tcrit, dt( tcrit, dfree), col = crukpink, lwd = 1.4)
text(-(tcrit + 0.30), 0.072, "2.5%", col = crukpink, cex = 0.94, adj = c(0.5, 0))
text( (tcrit + 0.30), 0.072, "2.5%", col = crukpink, cex = 0.94, adj = c(0.5, 0))

## pink "Critical region" boxes, one over each tail
lab  <- "Critical region"
lcex <- 0.90
bw <- strwidth(lab, cex = lcex) * 1.18
bh <- strheight(lab, cex = lcex) * 1.5
for (sgn in c(-1, 1)) {
  bx <- sgn * 6.3; by <- ymax * 0.52
  rect(bx - bw/2, by - bh, bx + bw/2, by + bh,
       border = crukpink, lwd = 1.4, col = "white")
  text(bx, by, lab, col = crukpink, cex = lcex, font = 2)
  arrows(bx - sgn * bw/2 * 0.75, by - bh, sgn * (tcrit + 1.0), 0.012,
         length = 0.05, lwd = 1.2, col = crukpink)
}

## the observed statistic, sitting on the axis
points(tobs, 0, pch = 19, col = cruklight, cex = 1.7)
text(tobs - 0.3, 0.030, expression(italic(t[s]) == 9.19), col = cruklight,
     cex = 1.0, font = 2, adj = c(1, 0))

## light-blue "p-value" box, with an arrow to each hatched tail
lab1 <- expression(bold("Two-sided ") * bolditalic(p) * bold("-value"))
lab2 <- expression(bold("= 0.0003"))
bx <- 0; by <- ymax * 1.12
gap <- strheight("X", cex = lcex) * 1.35
bw2 <- strwidth(lab1, cex = lcex) * 1.12
bh2 <- strheight("X", cex = lcex) * 1.75
rect(bx - bw2/2, by - bh2, bx + bw2/2, by + bh2,
     border = cruklight, lwd = 1.4, col = "white")
text(bx, by + gap/2, lab1, col = cruklight, cex = lcex)
text(bx, by - gap/2, lab2, col = cruklight, cex = lcex)
for (sgn in c(-1, 1))
  arrows(sgn * bw2/2, by - bh2 * 0.55, sgn * 8.0, 0.009,
         length = 0.05, lwd = 1.2, col = cruklight)

text(0, ymax * 1.40, expression(italic(t) ~ "distribution," ~ df == 5),
     col = crukdark, cex = 1.0)
dev.off()
```

## The multiple testing problem {.t}

```{r tdist-family, include=FALSE}
crukdark <- "#00007E"
crukpink <- "#FF0087"

pdf("t-distribution-family.pdf", width = 6.86, height = 3.0)
layout(matrix(1:4, nrow = 1), widths = c(1, 1, 0.28, 1))
par(mar = c(2.6, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5), mgp = c(1.5, 0.45, 0), cex = 1)

panel <- function(dens, xlim, lo, hi, ticks, title, lab = NULL) {
  xs <- seq(xlim[1], xlim[2], length.out = 1200)
  ys <- dens(xs)
  ys[!is.finite(ys)] <- NA
  ymax <- max(ys, na.rm = TRUE)
  plot(NULL, xlim = xlim, ylim = c(0, ymax * 1.18),
       axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  ## rejection regions: below lo and/or above hi
  if (!is.na(lo)) {
    xl <- seq(xlim[1], lo, length.out = 300)
    polygon(c(xl, rev(xl)), c(dens(xl), rep(0, length(xl))),
            col = crukpink, border = NA)
  }
  xr <- seq(hi, xlim[2], length.out = 300)
  polygon(c(xr, rev(xr)), c(dens(xr), rep(0, length(xr))),
          col = crukpink, border = NA)
  lines(xs, ys, col = crukdark, lwd = 2)
  if (!is.null(lab)) {
    segments(hi, 0, hi, dens(hi), col = crukpink, lwd = 1.4)
    text(hi + 0.03 * diff(xlim), dens(hi) + 0.12 * ymax, lab, col = crukpink,
         cex = 0.96, adj = c(0, 0.5))
    if (!is.na(lo)) {
      segments(lo, 0, lo, dens(lo), col = crukpink, lwd = 1.4)
      text(lo - 0.03 * diff(xlim), dens(lo) + 0.12 * ymax, lab, col = crukpink,
           cex = 0.96, adj = c(1, 0.5))
    }
  }
  axis(1, at = ticks, cex.axis = 1.02, lwd = 1.1)
  text(mean(xlim), ymax * 1.13, title, col = crukdark, cex = 1.03, xpd = NA)
}

## t_1: normal, two-sided 2.5% tails
panel(dnorm, c(-4, 4), qnorm(0.025), qnorm(0.975), c(-3, 0, 3),
      expression(italic(t)[1] ~ "~" ~ N(0, 1)), lab = "2.5%")

## t_2: F distribution, upper 5% tail
panel(function(x) df(x, 4, 20), c(0, 10), NA, qf(0.95, 4, 20), c(0, 3, 6, 9),
      expression(italic(t)[2] ~ "~" ~ F[list(4, 20)]), lab = "5%")

## dots standing in for t_3, ..., t_(n-1)
plot.new()
text(0.5, 0.45, expression(cdots), col = crukdark, cex = 2)

## t_n: chi-square, upper 5% tail
panel(function(x) dchisq(x, 6), c(0, 28), NA, qchisq(0.95, 6), c(0, 7, 14, 21, 28),
      expression(italic(t)[n] ~ "~" ~ chi[6]^2), lab = "5%")
dev.off()
```

\vspace*{\dimexpr0.5em-1pt\relax}

\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\begin{column}{0.335\textwidth}
\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{Single null hypothesis}}

\vspace{0.4em}

{\small Let $H_0$ be a null hypothesis\par}
\end{column}
\begin{column}{0.635\textwidth}
\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{Family of null hypotheses}}

\vspace{0.4em}

{\small Let $\mathcal{F} = \{H_1, H_2, \dots, H_n\}$ be a family of null hypotheses\par}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

\vspace{0.5em}

\begingroup\centering\small
We apply a statistical test to $H_0$ and to each $H_i \in \mathcal{F}$\par
\vspace{0.2em}
Under each null hypothesis, the distribution of its test statistic is known:\par
\endgroup

\vspace{-4.5pt}

\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\begin{column}{0.335\textwidth}
\centering\includegraphics[height=0.27\textheight]{t-distribution-generic.pdf}
\end{column}
\begin{column}{0.635\textwidth}
\centering\includegraphics[height=0.27\textheight]{t-distribution-family.pdf}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

\vspace{7.5pt}

\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\begin{column}{0.335\textwidth}
{\small If $H_0$ is \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE}, the probability of a false positive statement is 5\%\par}
\end{column}
\begin{column}{0.635\textwidth}
{\small If all the $H_i$, $i = 1, 2, \dots, n$, are \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE}, the probability of at least one false positive statement (FWER) is~$\geq$~5\% and depends on the joint distribution of the test statistics $t_i$\par}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

\par\endgroup

\vfill
\begingroup\centering
\textbf{\large If we go on testing long enough, we will inevitably find\\ something that is ``statistically significant''}\par
\vspace{0.4em}
\textbf{\large A $p$-value controls the error rate of \emph{its own} test,\\ not that of the whole family}\par\endgroup
\vspace*{0.8em}

```{r process-flow-stage2, fig.width=6.6, fig.height=3.15, fig.align="center"}
draw_roadmap(highlight = 2)
```

\vspace{-0.3em}

\noindent\hspace*{0.051\linewidth}\footnotesize\textbf{FWER}: Family-Wise Error Rate \newline \hspace*{0.051\linewidth}\textbf{FDR}: False Discovery Rate\normalsize

## Family-Wise Error Rate (FWER) {.t}

\vspace{-6pt}

Let $\mathcal{F} = \{H_1, H_2, \dots, H_n\}$ be a finite family of null hypotheses, and let $m_0$ ($0 \le m_0 \le n$) denote the number of \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE} \textbf{null hypotheses}.

\vspace{-0.4em}

\begin{center}
\normalsize
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\hline
$\mathcal{F}$ & Not Rejected & Rejected & Total \\
\hline
\colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE}  & \color{crukdark}$U$ & \colorbox{crukpink}{\color{crukdark}$V$} & $m_0$ \\
\colorbox{green}{\color{black}FALSE} & \color{crukdark}$T$ & \color{crukdark}$S$ & $n - m_0$ \\
\hline
Total & \color{crukdark}$n - R$ & \color{crukdark}$R$ & $n$ \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\begingroup
\setlength{\leftmargini}{0pt}

\hangindent=9pt\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Because the test statistics follow a probability distribution, the counts \color{crukdark}$U$\color{black}, \color{crukdark}$V$\color{black}, \color{crukdark}$T$\color{black}, \color{crukdark}$S$\color{black}, \color{crukdark}$n-R$ \color{black} and \color{crukdark}$R$ \color{black} also follow probability distributions (i.e.\ they are random variables). The quantities \color{crukdark}$n-R$ \color{black} and \color{crukdark}$R$ \color{black} are observable

\hangindent=9pt\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ The counts $m_0$, $n-m_0$ and $n$ are \textbf{fixed}, not random: $n$ is known, whereas $m_0$ and $n-m_0$ are \textbf{unknown}

\endgroup

\vspace{-0.3em}

\begin{center}
\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{\large FWER $\boldsymbol{:=}$ P(\colorbox{crukpink}{$V$} > 0)}}
\end{center}

\vspace{-0.95em}

\begingroup\centering
We want to control the FWER \textbf{whatever $\boldsymbol{m_0}$ is} and whichever nulls are \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE}.\par\vspace{-\parskip}
\textbf{We accept only a small probability $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$ (e.g.\ 0.05) of at least one false positive!!!}\par
\endgroup

## FWER and raw $p$-values {.t}

\vspace{-0.01em}

\begingroup
\setlength{\leftmargini}{0pt}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Let $\mathcal{F} = \{H_1, H_2, \dots, H_n\}$ be a finite family of \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE} null hypotheses: this is the \textbf{global null hypothesis}, $H_0^{\mathrm{global}}$\par

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Each hypothesis is tested at a pre-specified significance level $\alpha$

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Assuming the $n$ tests are \textbf{independent}, FWER = $1 - (1-\alpha)^n$

\endgroup

```{r fwer-plot, fig.width=6.2, fig.height=3.4, fig.align="center", out.width="79%"}
n      <- 0:100
alphas <- c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001)
cols   <- c("#FF0087", "#009CEE", "#00007E")
labs   <- c(expression(alpha == 0.05), expression(alpha == 0.01),
            expression(alpha == 0.001))

par(mar = c(2.6, 4.6, 0.6, 10.6), mgp = c(2.2, 0.5, 0), xpd = FALSE)
plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 100), ylim = c(0, 1), bty = "n", las = 1, xaxt = "n",
     xaxs = "i", xlab = "",
     ylab = "actual FWER", cex.axis = 0.9, cex.lab = 1.4)
axis(1, at = seq(0, 100, 20), cex.axis = 0.9)

abline(h = seq(0, 1, 0.25), col = "grey88", lwd = 0.8)
abline(h = 0.05, col = "grey55", lwd = 1, lty = 2)
text(101.5, 0.05, "nominal FWER = 0.05", col = "grey35", cex = 1.15, adj = c(0, 0.5), xpd = NA)

for (i in seq_along(alphas)) {
  lines(n, 1 - (1 - alphas[i])^n, col = cols[i], lwd = 2.2)
}

par(xpd = NA)
mtext(expression(italic(n)), side = 1, line = 0.5, at = 108, cex = 1.4, las = 1)

legend(x = 108, y = 0.55, legend = labs, col = cols, lwd = 2.2,
       bty = "n", cex = 1.2, seg.len = 1.6, text.col = "grey15",
       y.intersp = 1.5, xjust = 0, yjust = 0.5)
```

## FWER and raw $p$-values {.t}

\vspace{-2.79pt}

Ventricular shortening velocity (VSV, %/s) and fasting blood glucose (FBG, mmol/l) were measured in 24 type 1 diabetic patients (23 with complete data). The following two null hypotheses are tested:

$H_1$: $\mu_{\mathrm{VSV}} = 0$ at FBG = 0

$H_2$: no linear association between FBG and VSV (i.e.\ slope = 0)

\vspace{-1.0em}

\begin{columns}[T]
\begin{column}{0.27\linewidth}
\vspace{3.0em}
A simple linear model\\is used to test\\both hypotheses
\end{column}
\begin{column}{0.73\linewidth}

```{r thuesen-plot, fig.width=4.2, fig.height=3.15, fig.align="left", out.width="42%", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(ISwR)
data(thuesen)
thuesen <- thuesen[complete.cases(thuesen), ]

fit <- lm(short.velocity ~ blood.glucose, data = thuesen)

par(mar = c(3.1, 3.5, 0.4, 1.0), mgp = c(2.0, 0.6, 0))
plot(thuesen$blood.glucose, thuesen$short.velocity, type = "n", bty = "n", las = 1,
     xlim = c(0, 20), ylim = c(0, max(thuesen$short.velocity)),
     xlab = "FBG (mmol/l)", ylab = "VSV (%/s)",
     cex.axis = 0.85, cex.lab = 0.9)
grid(nx = NA, ny = NULL, col = "grey90", lty = 1, lwd = 0.8)

points(thuesen$blood.glucose, thuesen$short.velocity, pch = 21, cex = 0.85, lwd = 1.1,
       col = "#00007E", bg = "white")
xs <- c(0, 20)
lines(xs, predict(fit, data.frame(blood.glucose = xs)), col = "#FF0087", lwd = 2.4)
```

\end{column}
\end{columns}

\vspace{-0.5em}
\scriptsize


## Adjustment of raw $p$-values

\vspace{-10.47pt}

```{r padjust-plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.12, fig.align="center"}
circle <- function(cx, cy, r, n = 300) {
  theta <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n)
  list(x = cx + r * cos(theta), y = cy + r * sin(theta))
}

curved_arrow <- function(x0, y0, x1, y1, bend = 0.25, ...) {
  t <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 100)
  mx <- (x0 + x1) / 2 - bend * (y1 - y0)
  my <- (y0 + y1) / 2 + bend * (x1 - x0)
  bx <- (1 - t)^2 * x0 + 2 * (1 - t) * t * mx + t^2 * x1
  by <- (1 - t)^2 * y0 + 2 * (1 - t) * t * my + t^2 * y1
  lines(bx, by, ...)
  arrows(bx[99], by[99], bx[100], by[100], length = 0.07, ...)
}

par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
plot(NULL, xlim = c(-7.85, 6.95), ylim = c(-3.90, 2.85), asp = 1,
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")

r_h <- 2.75
r_t <- 2.20
r_p <- 1.84

cx_h <- -5.00
cx_t <- 0.45
cx_p <- 4.99

polygon(circle(cx_h, 0, r_h), border = "black", lwd = 2)
polygon(circle(cx_t, 0, r_t), border = "black", lwd = 2)
polygon(circle(cx_p, 0, r_p), border = "black", lwd = 2)

labs_h <- c(expression(italic(H)[1]), expression(italic(H)[2]), "...",
            expression(italic(H)[italic(n)]))
labs_t <- c(expression(italic(t)[1]), expression(italic(t)[2]), "...",
            expression(italic(t)[italic(n)]))
labs_p <- c(expression(italic(p)[1]), expression(italic(p)[2]), "...",
            expression(italic(p)[italic(n)]))
ys <- c(1.56, 0.55, -0.46, -1.56)

for (i in seq_along(ys)) {
  text(cx_h, ys[i], labs_h[[i]], cex = 1.4)
  text(cx_t, ys[i], labs_t[[i]], cex = 1.4)
  text(cx_p, ys[i], labs_p[[i]], cex = 1.4)
  if (labs_h[[i]] != "...") {
    curved_arrow(cx_h + 0.62, ys[i], cx_t - 0.56, ys[i],
                 bend = 0.12, col = "gray35", lwd = 1.4)
    curved_arrow(cx_t + 0.56, ys[i], cx_p - 0.56, ys[i],
                 bend = 0.12, col = "gray35", lwd = 1.4)
  }
}

draw_check <- function(cx, cy, s = 0.35, ...) {
  lines(c(cx - s, cx - 0.15 * s, cx + s),
        c(cy + 0.1 * s, cy - 0.8 * s, cy + s), ...)
}

draw_cross <- function(cx, cy, s = 0.32, ...) {
  lines(c(cx - s, cx + s), c(cy - s, cy + s), ...)
  lines(c(cx - s, cx + s), c(cy + s, cy - s), ...)
}

y_mark <- -r_h - 0.95

draw_check(cx_h, y_mark, s = 0.50, col = "#009CEE", lwd = 5, lend = 1)
draw_cross(cx_t, y_mark, s = 0.45, col = "#FF0087", lwd = 5, lend = 1)
draw_check(cx_p, y_mark, s = 0.50, col = "#009CEE", lwd = 5, lend = 1)
```

\vspace{-0.5em}

\begingroup
\setlength{\leftmargini}{0pt}
\justifying

Here we do not use the multivariate distribution of the test statistics ($t_1, t_2, \ldots, t_n$), working instead with the marginal $p$-values ($p_i$) of the individual null hypotheses ($H_i$).

\endgroup

## Bonferroni correction

\vspace{0.1em}

\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{\Large Boole's inequality}}

\noindent Let $E_1, E_2,\ldots,E_n$ be events.

\vspace{-0.4em}

\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\column{0.5\textwidth}

\vspace{0.35em}

$\mathrm{P}\left(\bigcup\limits_{i=1}^{n} E_i\right) \le \sum\limits_{i=1}^{n} \mathrm{P}(E_i)$

\column{0.5\textwidth}

\vspace{\baselineskip}
\vspace{-6.50em}

```{r venn-ellipses, fig.width=2.6, fig.height=1.56, fig.align="center"}
ellipse_points <- function(cx, cy, a, b, angle = 0, n = 200) {
  theta <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n)
  x <- a * cos(theta)
  y <- b * sin(theta)
  rad <- angle * pi / 180
  data.frame(
    x = x * cos(rad) - y * sin(rad) + cx,
    y = x * sin(rad) + y * cos(rad) + cy
  )
}

in_ellipse <- function(px, py, cx, cy, a, b, angle = 0) {
  rad <- angle * pi / 180
  dx <- px - cx
  dy <- py - cy
  xr <- dx * cos(-rad) - dy * sin(-rad)
  yr <- dx * sin(-rad) + dy * cos(-rad)
  (xr / a)^2 + (yr / b)^2 <= 1
}

par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
plot(NULL, xlim = c(-3, 3), ylim = c(-2.6, 2.4), asp = 1, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")

e1 <- ellipse_points(-0.7, 0.5, 1.8, 1.1, angle = 30)
e2 <- ellipse_points(0.7, 0.5, 1.8, 1.1, angle = -30)
e3 <- ellipse_points(0, -0.8, 1.8, 1.1, angle = 90)

polygon(e1, border = "black", lwd = 2)
polygon(e2, border = "black", lwd = 2)
polygon(e3, border = "black", lwd = 2)

grid <- expand.grid(x = seq(-3, 3, length.out = 300), y = seq(-2.6, 2.4, length.out = 300))
in1 <- with(grid, in_ellipse(x, y, -0.7, 0.5, 1.8, 1.1, 30))
in2 <- with(grid, in_ellipse(x, y, 0.7, 0.5, 1.8, 1.1, -30))
in3 <- with(grid, in_ellipse(x, y, 0, -0.8, 1.8, 1.1, 90))

center <- colMeans(grid[in1 & in2 & in3, ])
centroid1 <- colMeans(grid[in1 & !in2 & !in3, ])
centroid2 <- colMeans(grid[in2 & !in1 & !in3, ])
centroid3 <- colMeans(grid[in3 & !in1 & !in2, ])

text(centroid1["x"], centroid1["y"], expression(italic(E)[1]), cex = 1.4)
text(centroid2["x"], centroid2["y"], expression(italic(E)[2]), cex = 1.4)
text(centroid3["x"], centroid3["y"], expression(italic(E)[italic(n)]), cex = 1.4)
text(center["x"], center["y"], "...", cex = 1.4, font = 2)
```

\end{columns}

\begingroup
\setlength{\leftmargini}{0pt}

\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{\Large Boole's inequality is applied in hypothesis testing}}

$E_i$ := \{Under a \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE} $H_i$, the test statistic $t_i$ falls inside the \fcolorbox{crukpink}{white}{\textcolor{crukpink}{\textbf{critical region}}}\}

\vspace{-0.70em}

FWER = $\mathrm{P}\left(\bigcup\limits_{i \in K_0} E_i\right)$ \hspace{0.6em} ($K_0$ = set of the $m_0$ \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE} null hypotheses)

\vspace{-0.55em}

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ We want FWER $\leq \alpha$ (e.g.\ 0.05)

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Each test is run at level $\frac{\alpha}{n}$, so $\mathrm{P}(E_i) = \frac{\alpha}{n}$ for every $i \in K_0$

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Hence, FWER $\leq \sum\limits_{i \in K_0} \mathrm{P}(E_i) = \frac{\alpha}{n} \times m_0 \leq \alpha$

\endgroup

## Bonferroni correction {.t}

\vspace{\dimexpr-0.72em+1.335pt\relax}\parskip=\dimexpr\parskip\relax plus \gluestretch\parskip

Ventricular shortening velocity (VSV, %/s) and fasting blood glucose (FBG, mmol/l) were measured in 24 type 1 diabetic patients (23 with complete data). The following two null hypotheses are tested:

$H_1$: $\mu_{\mathrm{VSV}} = 0$ at FBG = 0

$H_2$: no linear association between FBG and VSV (i.e.\ slope = 0)

\vspace{-0.5em}
\scriptsize\topsep=\dimexpr\topsep\relax plus \gluestretch\topsep\partopsep=\dimexpr\partopsep\relax plus \gluestretch\partopsep

```{r thuesen-lm-bonferroni, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(ISwR)
data(thuesen)
thuesen <- thuesen[complete.cases(thuesen), ]
cf <- summary(lm(short.velocity ~ blood.glucose, data = thuesen))$coefficients
padj <- format.pval(p.adjust(cf[, 4], method = "bonferroni"), eps = 0.001, digits = 2)
noquote(cbind(formatC(cf[, 1:3], format = "f", digits = 3), "Pr(>|t|)" = format.pval(cf[, 4], eps = 0.001, digits = 2)))
```

\normalsize

\vspace{-1.3em}

\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{Correction rule}}

\vspace{-0.3em}

\noindent{\small%
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.0}%
\begin{tabular}{@{}l@{\hspace{3em}}l}
\textbf{Raw $\boldsymbol{p}$-values} & \textbf{Adjusted $\boldsymbol{p}$-values} \\
$p_1$ & $n \times p_1$ \\
$p_2$ & $n \times p_2$ \\
$\vdots$ & $\vdots$ \\
$p_n$ & $n \times p_n$ \\
\end{tabular}\par}

## Holm--Bonferroni correction

\vspace{1pt}

\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{\Large We apply Boole's inequality in a step-down procedure}}

\hangindent=9pt\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Order the $n$ $p$-values: $p_{(1)} \leq p_{(2)} \leq \ldots \leq p_{(n)}$, with corresponding hypotheses $H_{(1)}, H_{(2)}, \ldots, H_{(n)}$

```{r holm-steps, fig.width=7.4, fig.height=2.05, fig.align="center"}
crukdark  <- "#00007E"
cruklight <- "#009CEE"
crukpink  <- "#FF0087"

labs <- list(expression(italic(p)[(1)]), expression(italic(p)[(2)]),
             expression(ldots), expression(italic(p)[(italic(n) - 1)]),
             expression(italic(p)[(italic(n))]))
starts <- c(1, 2, 5)
steps  <- list(expression(bold("Step 1")), expression(bold("Step 2")),
               expression(bold("Step") ~ bolditalic(n)))
thr    <- list(quote(alpha / italic(n)), quote(alpha / (italic(n) - 1)),
               quote(alpha))

yc <- c(2.55, 1.75, 0.35)
h  <- 0.40

par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
plot(NULL, xlim = c(-1.70, 7.20), ylim = c(-0.10, 3.00), asp = 1,
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")

for (r in seq_along(starts)) {
  s <- starts[r]
  text(-1.70, yc[r], steps[[r]], adj = c(0, 0.5), cex = 1.35, col = "black")
  for (i in s:5) {
    on <- (i == s)
    rect(i - 1, yc[r] - h, i, yc[r] + h,
         col = if (on) cruklight else "grey93",
         border = if (on) crukdark else "grey60",
         lwd = if (on) 2 else 1.1)
    text(i - 0.5, yc[r], labs[[i]], cex = 1.2,
         col = if (on) crukpink else "black")
  }
  text(5.18, yc[r], bquote("" <= .(thr[[r]])), adj = c(0, 0.5),
       cex = 1.35, col = crukpink)
}

ydots <- c(0.85, 1.05, 1.25)
points(rep(4.5, 3),  ydots, pch = 19, cex = 0.45, col = "grey45")
points(rep(-1.30, 3), ydots, pch = 19, cex = 0.45, col = crukdark)
```

\vspace{-0.7em}

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Stop at the first non-rejection: the remaining hypotheses are all retained

\textbf{It controls the FWER at the $\alpha$ level}, but it is less conservative than Bonferroni because the threshold \textbf{grows} after each rejection ($\frac{\alpha}{n}, \frac{\alpha}{n-1}, \frac{\alpha}{n-2}, \dots$), whereas Bonferroni uses $\frac{\alpha}{n}$ throughout.

## Holm--Bonferroni correction {.t}

\vspace{\dimexpr-0.82em-4.42pt\relax}\parskip=\dimexpr\parskip\relax plus \gluestretch\parskip

Ventricular shortening velocity (VSV, %/s) and fasting blood glucose (FBG, mmol/l) were measured in 24 type 1 diabetic patients (23 with complete data). The following two null hypotheses are tested:

$H_1$: $\mu_{\mathrm{VSV}} = 0$ at FBG = 0

$H_2$: no linear association between FBG and VSV (i.e.\ slope = 0)

\vspace{-0.5em}
\scriptsize\topsep=\dimexpr\topsep\relax plus \gluestretch\topsep\partopsep=\dimexpr\partopsep\relax plus \gluestretch\partopsep

```{r thuesen-lm-holm, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(ISwR)
data(thuesen)
thuesen <- thuesen[complete.cases(thuesen), ]
cf <- summary(lm(short.velocity ~ blood.glucose, data = thuesen))$coefficients
padjh <- format.pval(p.adjust(cf[, 4], method = "holm"), eps = 0.001, digits = 2)
noquote(cbind(formatC(cf[, 1:3], format = "f", digits = 3), "Pr(>|t|)" = format.pval(cf[, 4], eps = 0.001, digits = 2)))
```

\vspace{-2.1em}

\noindent\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{Correction rule}}

\vspace{-0.5em}

\noindent{\small Order the $n$ $p$-values: $p_{(1)} \leq p_{(2)} \leq \ldots \leq p_{(n)}$\par}

\vspace{-0.3em}

\noindent{\small%
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.0}%
\begin{tabular}{@{}l@{\hspace{3em}}l}
\textbf{Raw $\boldsymbol{p}$-values} & \textbf{Adjusted $\boldsymbol{p}$-values} \\
$p_{(1)}$ & $n \times p_{(1)}$ \\
$p_{(2)}$ & $(n - 1) \times p_{(2)}$ \\
$\vdots$ & $\vdots$ \\
$p_{(n)}$ & $1 \times p_{(n)}$ \\
\end{tabular}\par}

## Assumptions on test statistic relationships

\vspace{-11.57pt}

```{r padjust-plot-2, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.12, fig.align="center"}

  theta <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n)

}

  t <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 100)
  mx <- (x0 + x1) / 2 - bend * (y1 - y0)
  my <- (y0 + y1) / 2 + bend * (x1 - x0)
  bx <- (1 - t)^2 * x0 + 2 * (1 - t) * t * mx + t^2 * x1
  by <- (1 - t)^2 * y0 + 2 * (1 - t) * t * my + t^2 * y1
  lines(bx, by, ...)
  arrows(bx[99], by[99], bx[100], by[100], length = 0.07, ...)
}

par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
plot(NULL, xlim = c(-7.85, 6.95), ylim = c(-3.90, 2.85), asp = 1,
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")

r_h <- 2.75
r_t <- 2.20
r_p <- 1.84

cx_t <- 0.45
cx_p <- 4.99

polygon(circle(cx_t, 0, r_t), border = "black", lwd = 2)
polygon(circle(cx_p, 0, r_p), border = "black", lwd = 2)

            expression(italic(H)[italic(n)]))
labs_t <- c(expression(italic(t)[1]), expression(italic(t)[2]), "...",
            expression(italic(t)[italic(n)]))

  text(cx_p, ys[i], labs_p[[i]], cex = 1.4)
  if (labs_h[[i]] != "...") {

  lines(c(cx - s, cx - 0.15 * s, cx + s),
        c(cy + 0.1 * s, cy - 0.8 * s, cy + s), ...)
}

```

\vspace{-0.5em}

\begingroup
\setlength{\leftmargini}{0pt}
\justifying

The corrections differ in what they assume about the \textbf{dependence} among the test statistics ($t_1, t_2, \ldots, t_n$): Bonferroni and Holm require \textbf{no assumption} about it, while Šidák assumes \textbf{independence}.

\endgroup

## Šidák correction

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Let $H_1, H_2, \dots, H_n$ be hypotheses with **independent** test statistics $t_1, t_2, \dots, t_n$

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ For each $H_i$, $i = 1, 2, \dots, n$, set the significance level to $\alpha_{\text{Šidák}}$. Under $H_0^{\mathrm{global}}$, $$\mathrm{FWER} = 1 - (1-\alpha_\text{Šidák})^{n}$$

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Set the FWER equal to $\alpha$. Solving the previous equation for $\alpha_\text{Šidák}$, we obtain the individual significance level for each hypothesis $H_i$:\par
\vspace{0.98em}
\centerline{$\displaystyle\textcolor{crukdark}{\boldsymbol{\alpha_\text{Šidák} = 1 - (1-\alpha)^\frac{1}{n}}}$}

\vspace{-0.07em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Reject $H_i$ if $p_i \leq \alpha_\text{Šidák}$, or equivalently if the adjusted $p$-value\newline $\tilde{p}_i = 1 - (1 - p_i)^{n} \leq \alpha$\par

\vspace{0.6em}

The Šidák correction is valid and, since $1-(1-\alpha)^{1/n} > \alpha/n$ for $n \geq 2$, it is slightly more powerful than the Bonferroni correction

## Holm--Šidák correction

\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{\Large We apply the Šidák correction in a step-down procedure}}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Order the $n$ $p$-values: $p_{(1)} \leq p_{(2)} \leq \ldots \leq p_{(n)}$, with corresponding hypotheses $H_{(1)}, H_{(2)}, \ldots, H_{(n)}$ (\textbf{independent} test statistics)

```{r holm-sidak-steps, fig.width=7.4, fig.height=2.05, fig.align="center"}
crukdark  <- "#00007E"
cruklight <- "#009CEE"
crukpink  <- "#FF0087"

labs <- list(expression(italic(p)[(1)]), expression(italic(p)[(2)]),
             expression(ldots), expression(italic(p)[(italic(n) - 1)]),
             expression(italic(p)[(italic(n))]))
starts <- c(1, 2, 5)
steps  <- list(expression(bold("Step 1")), expression(bold("Step 2")),
               expression(bold("Step") ~ bolditalic(n)))
thr    <- list(quote(1 - (1 - alpha)^{1/italic(n)}),
               quote(1 - (1 - alpha)^{1/(italic(n) - 1)}),
               quote(alpha))

yc <- c(2.55, 1.75, 0.35)
h  <- 0.40

par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
plot(NULL, xlim = c(-1.70, 7.20), ylim = c(-0.10, 3.00), asp = 1,
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")

for (r in seq_along(starts)) {
  s <- starts[r]
  text(-1.70, yc[r], steps[[r]], adj = c(0, 0.5), cex = 1.35, col = "black")
  for (i in s:5) {
    on <- (i == s)
    rect(i - 1, yc[r] - h, i, yc[r] + h,
         col = if (on) cruklight else "grey93",
         border = if (on) crukdark else "grey60",
         lwd = if (on) 2 else 1.1)
    text(i - 0.5, yc[r], labs[[i]], cex = 1.2,
         col = if (on) crukpink else "black")
  }
  text(5.18, yc[r], bquote("" <= .(thr[[r]])), adj = c(0, 0.5),
       cex = 1.20, col = crukpink)
}

ydots <- c(0.85, 1.05, 1.25)
points(rep(4.5, 3),  ydots, pch = 19, cex = 0.45, col = "grey45")
points(rep(-1.30, 3), ydots, pch = 19, cex = 0.45, col = crukdark)
```

\vspace{-0.7em}

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Stop at the first non-rejection: the remaining hypotheses are all retained

\textbf{It controls the FWER at the $\alpha$ level} under independence, and it is slightly less conservative than Holm--Bonferroni since $1-(1-\alpha)^{1/j} \geq \alpha/j, \; j = 1, 2, \ldots, n$

## Which correction is the most powerful?

\vspace{\dimexpr-0.2em+1pt\relax}

All six procedures \textbf{control} the FWER at $\alpha$, each under its own condition. They differ in \textbf{how much power} they gain over Bonferroni, and in \textbf{what they must assume} to do so.

\vspace{-0.3em}

```{r power-ladder, fig.width=7.8, fig.height=2.9, fig.align="center"}
crukdark  <- "#00007E"
cruklight <- "#009CEE"
crukpink  <- "#FF0087"

labs <- c("Bonferroni", "Holm", "Šidák (single-step)", "Hochberg", "Hommel",
          "Holm–Šidák (step-down)")
x    <- c(1, 2, 1.6, 4, 5, 2.9)
y    <- c(1, 2.2, 1.05, 3.4, 4.3, 2.5)
## three assumption tiers, from least to most demanding:
##   dark blue  = none           (Bonferroni, Holm)
##   light blue = POD            (Sidak, Holm-Sidak)   -- positive orthant dependence
##   pink       = PRDS           (Hochberg, Hommel) -- PRDS implies POD, so it asks more
cols <- c(crukdark, crukdark, cruklight, crukpink, crukpink, cruklight)

par(mar = c(0, 0, 0.2, 0))
plot(NULL, xlim = c(0.35, 7.6), ylim = c(0.1, 4.9),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")

arrows(0.55, 0.55, 5.55, 0.55, length = 0.12, lwd = 2, col = "grey55")
text(3.05, 0.26, "increasing power", col = "grey35", cex = 0.95)

## every line joins a procedure to one that uniformly dominates it
segments(1, 1, 2, 2.2, col = "grey70", lwd = 1.6)
segments(2, 2.2, 4, 3.4, col = "grey70", lwd = 1.6)
segments(4, 3.4, 5, 4.3, col = "grey70", lwd = 1.6)
## Sidak is a side branch: it beats Bonferroni and is beaten by Holm-Sidak, but
## is not comparable with Holm, Hochberg or Hommel
segments(1, 1, 1.6, 1.05, col = "grey70", lwd = 1.6)
## Holm-Sidak is the step-down version of Sidak: it uniformly dominates BOTH Holm
## and Sidak (single-step), but is not comparable with Hochberg or Hommel
segments(2, 2.2, 2.9, 2.5, col = "grey70", lwd = 1.6)
segments(1.6, 1.05, 2.9, 2.5, col = "grey70", lwd = 1.6)

## the Sidak and Holm-Sidak labels are long, so they sit to the right of their
## points instead of above; Bonferroni's shifts left to clear its line to Holm
lab_dx  <- c(-0.2, 0, 0.24, 0, 0, 0.24)
lab_dy  <- c(0.34, 0.34, 0, 0.34, 0.34, 0)
lab_adj <- c(0.5, 0.5, 0, 0.5, 0.5, 0)
for (i in seq_along(labs)) {
  points(x[i], y[i], pch = 21, bg = cols[i], col = cols[i], cex = 2.2)
  text(x[i] + lab_dx[i], y[i] + lab_dy[i], labs[i], cex = 1.02, font = 2,
       col = cols[i], adj = c(lab_adj[i], 0.5))
}

## assumption legend, ordered from least to most demanding
text(6.15, 4.54, "SUFFICIENT CONDITION", col = "grey35", cex = 0.66, font = 2, adj = c(0, 0.5))
text(6.15, 4.16, "FOR FWER CONTROL", col = "grey35", cex = 0.66, font = 2, adj = c(0, 0.5))
## the three entries sit directly under the heading, left-aligned with it
text(6.33, 3.70, "none", col = crukdark, cex = 0.72, font = 2, adj = c(0, 0.5))
text(6.33, 3.28, "POD", col = cruklight, cex = 0.72, font = 2, adj = c(0, 0.5))
text(6.33, 2.86, "PRDS", col = crukpink, cex = 0.72, font = 2, adj = c(0, 0.5))
points(6.17, 3.70, pch = 21, bg = crukdark,  col = crukdark,  cex = 1.1)
points(6.17, 3.28, pch = 21, bg = cruklight, col = cruklight, cex = 1.1)
points(6.17, 2.86, pch = 21, bg = crukpink,  col = crukpink,  cex = 1.1)
```

\vspace{-0.2em}

\scriptsize

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textcolor{cruklight}{\textbf{Šidák (single-step)}} is \textbf{not uniformly more or less powerful} than \textbf{Holm}, \textbf{Hochberg} and \textbf{Hommel}: each can reject a hypothesis the other does not\par

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textcolor{cruklight}{\textbf{Šidák}}, \textcolor{cruklight}{\textbf{Holm–Šidák}}, \textcolor{crukpink}{\textbf{Hochberg}} and \textcolor{crukpink}{\textbf{Hommel}} all \textbf{control the FWER} when the test statistics are \textbf{independent}\par

\normalsize

## POD condition {.t}

\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{\Large POD $=$ Positive Orthant Dependence}}

\vspace{-0.4em}

```{r pod-only, fig.width=7.8, fig.height=2.6, fig.align="center"}
crukdark  <- "#00007E"
cruklight <- "#009CEE"
crukpink  <- "#FF0087"

cc <- 0.30            # an illustrative threshold c, big enough to be visible
set.seed(11)
n  <- 170

## a tick and a cross, drawn by hand so that they match the deck's other marks
mk_tick <- function(x, y, s, col) {
  lines(c(x - s, x - 0.2 * s, x + s), c(y + 0.15 * s, y - 0.8 * s, y + s),
        col = col, lwd = 2.4, lend = 1, xpd = NA)
}
mk_cross <- function(x, y, s, col) {
  lines(c(x - s, x + s), c(y - s, y + s), col = col, lwd = 2.4, lend = 1, xpd = NA)
  lines(c(x - s, x + s), c(y + s, y - s), col = col, lwd = 2.4, lend = 1, xpd = NA)
}

## a short label on a white patch, so it stays readable over the points
boxed_text <- function(x, y, lab, cex) {
  w <- strwidth(lab, cex = cex) / 2 + 0.015
  h <- strheight(lab, cex = cex) / 2 + 0.015
  rect(x - w, y - h, x + w, y + h, col = "white", border = NA)
  text(x, y, lab, cex = cex, font = 2, col = "grey30")
}

## top row: the joint picture of two true-null p-values, with the two corners
## POD talks about (both significant, both non-significant) shaded
pod_panel <- function(rho, corner = NULL) {
  z1 <- rnorm(n)
  z2 <- rho * z1 + sqrt(1 - rho^2) * rnorm(n)
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i",
       axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  rect(0, 0, cc, cc, col = "#D9EFFC", border = NA)
  rect(cc, cc, 1, 1, col = "#D9EFFC", border = NA)
  segments(cc, 0, cc, 1, col = "grey60", lty = 2)
  segments(0, cc, 1, cc, col = "grey60", lty = 2)
  points(pnorm(z1), pnorm(z2), pch = 16, cex = 0.7,
         col = adjustcolor(crukdark, 0.8))
  box(col = "grey45")
  ## the two orthant probabilities, as percentages, on a white patch
  z  <- matrix(rnorm(2e5), ncol = 2)
  zz <- cbind(z[, 1], rho * z[, 1] + sqrt(1 - rho^2) * z[, 2])
  q  <- qnorm(cc)
  pr <- c(mean(zz[, 1] < q & zz[, 2] < q), mean(zz[, 1] > q & zz[, 2] > q))
  for (k in 1:2) {
    px <- c(cc / 2, (1 + cc) / 2)[k]
    py <- c(cc / 2, (1 + cc) / 2)[k]
    lab <- sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * pr[k])
    cx <- 0.9
    if (!is.null(corner)) {
      ## stack the corner's name over its percentage, the pair centred in the box
      h1 <- strheight(corner[k], cex = 0.72) + 0.03
      h2 <- strheight(lab, cex = cx) + 0.04
      boxed_text(px, py + (h1 + h2) / 2 - h1 / 2, corner[k], 0.72)
      py <- py - (h1 + h2) / 2 + h2 / 2
    }
    rect(px - strwidth(lab, cex = cx) / 2 - 0.02,
         py - strheight(lab, cex = cx) / 2 - 0.02,
         px + strwidth(lab, cex = cx) / 2 + 0.02,
         py + strheight(lab, cex = cx) / 2 + 0.02,
         col = "white", border = NA)
    text(px, py, lab, cex = cx, font = 2, col = crukdark)
  }
}

## bottom row: the conditional picture PRDS talks about -- how likely the OTHER
## p-value is to be large, given that this true null's p-value equals u
prds_panel <- function(rho, col) {
  u <- seq(0.002, 0.998, length.out = 400)
  g <- if (rho == 0) rep(1 - cc, length(u)) else
    1 - pnorm((qnorm(cc) - rho * qnorm(u)) / sqrt(1 - rho^2))
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i",
       axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  abline(h = 1 - cc, col = "grey75", lty = 3)
  lines(u, g, lwd = 2.8, col = col)
  box(col = "grey45")
}


rhos <- c(0, 0.85, -0.85)
hdr  <- c("independent", "move together", "opposite sides")
hcol <- c("grey35", cruklight, crukpink)

draw_pod_row <- function(mar = c(1.35, 0.2, 1.75, 0.2)) {
  set.seed(11)
  par(mar = mar)
  plot.new()
  text(0.3, 0.5, "POD", srt = 90, font = 2, cex = 1.55, col = cruklight)
  for (i in 1:3) {
    par(mar = mar)
    ## the first panel also names the two shaded corners
    pod_panel(rhos[i], corner = if (i == 1) c("both sig.", "both non-sig."))
    if (i == 1) {
      ## and shows where the threshold c is
      text(cc, -0.105, expression(italic(c)), cex = 1.15, xpd = NA)
      text(-0.085, cc, expression(italic(c)), cex = 1.15, xpd = NA)
    }
    mtext(hdr[i], side = 3, line = 0.30, cex = 1.12, font = 2, col = hcol[i])
    if (i == 3) mk_cross(0.075, 1.115, 0.05, crukpink) else
      mk_tick(0.075, 1.115, 0.055, hcol[i])
    text(0.5, -0.105, expression(italic(p)[1]), cex = 1.15, xpd = NA)
    if (i == 1)
      text(-0.085, 0.5, expression(italic(p)[2]), srt = 90, cex = 1.15, xpd = NA)
  }
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0)); plot.new()
}

draw_prds_row <- function() {
  par(mar = c(1.95, 0.2, 0.85, 0.2))
  plot.new()
  text(0.3, 0.5, "PRDS", srt = 90, font = 2, cex = 1.55, col = crukpink)
  pcol <- c("grey45", cruklight, crukpink)
  for (i in 1:3) {
    par(mar = c(1.95, 0.2, 0.85, 0.2))
    prds_panel(rhos[i], pcol[i])
    ## say in one word what the curve does: this IS the PRDS condition.
    ## dead centre of the box, so the three verdicts line up across the row
    text(0.5, 0.5,
         c("flat", "increasing", "decreasing")[i], cex = 1.05, font = 2,
         col = pcol[i])
    if (i == 1)
      text(0.035, 0.95,
           expression("P(other " * italic(p) * " > " * italic(c) * "  |  " *
                      italic(p)[1] * " = " * italic(u) * ")"),
           adj = c(0, 1), cex = 1.0, col = "grey35")
    text(0.5, -0.115, expression(italic(u)), cex = 1.15, xpd = NA)
  }
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0)); plot.new()
}

## only the POD row on this slide
layout(matrix(1:5, nrow = 1), widths = c(0.3, 1, 1, 1, 0.06))
## a taller panel pushes the outside labels further out, so give them more room
draw_pod_row(c(2.3, 0.2, 2.8, 0.2))
```

\vspace{-0.9em}

\begingroup
\fontsize{8.6}{10.2}\selectfont
\setlength{\parskip}{3pt}

\centerline{$c$ $=$ the \textbf{significance level} each $p$-value is compared with (e.g.\ 0.05)}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textbf{POD}: }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textcolor{cruklight}{\textbf{POD}}: for \textbf{any} threshold $c$ (e.g.\ 0.05), the \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE} null $p$-values are \textbf{at least as likely} to be \textbf{all significant} (i.e.\ \textbf{at the same time}), \textbf{and} at least as likely to be \textbf{all non-significant} (i.e.\ \textbf{at the same time}), \textbf{as if they were independent}: $P(\text{all } p_i \le c) \ge \prod_i P(p_i \le c)$ and $P(\text{all } p_i > c) \ge \prod_i P(p_i > c)$. \textcolor{cruklight}{\textbf{Šidák}} needs \textbf{only} the second one (positive upper orthant dependence, PUOD): $\text{FWER} = 1 - P(\text{all } p_i > c) \le 1 - (1-c)^{m_0} \le \alpha$ \textbf{(all together, not one given another)}\par

\endgroup

## PRDS condition {.t}

\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{\Large PRDS $=$ Positive Regression Dependence on a Subset}}

\vspace{-0.4em}

```{r prds-both, fig.width=7.8, fig.height=2.85, fig.align="center"}
## both rows here, so the conditional picture can be read against the joint one
layout(matrix(1:10, nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE), widths = c(0.3, 1, 1, 1, 0.06))
draw_pod_row()
draw_prds_row()
```

\vspace{-1.1em}

\begingroup
\fontsize{8.6}{10.2}\selectfont
\setlength{\parskip}{3pt}

\centerline{$u$ $=$ a \textbf{possible value taken} by the $p$-value of a \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE} null $H_i$, $u \in [0, 1]$}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textbf{PRDS}: }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textcolor{crukpink}{\textbf{PRDS}}: \textcolor{cruklight}{\textbf{POD}} compares \textbf{one unconditional joint probability} with the \textbf{independent} case, while \textcolor{crukpink}{\textbf{PRDS}} requires that, \underline{\textbf{for each} \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE} \textbf{null}} $H_i$, $i \in K_0$, the probability that the \textbf{other} $p$-values fall \textbf{outside the critical region} be \textbf{non-decreasing in} $u$, \textbf{at every} $u$. \textbf{Sufficient} for \textcolor{crukpink}{\textbf{Hochberg}} and \textcolor{crukpink}{\textbf{Hommel}}, and for \textbf{BH} to control the \textbf{FDR}\par

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textbf{PRDS implies POD}, but \textbf{not} the converse\par

\endgroup

\normalsize

## Joint distribution of the test statistics {.t}

\vspace{-0.82em}\parskip=\dimexpr\parskip\relax plus \gluestretch\parskip

Ventricular shortening velocity (VSV, %/s) and fasting blood glucose (FBG, mmol/l) were measured in 24 type 1 diabetic patients (23 with complete data). The following two null hypotheses are tested:

$H_1$: $\mu_{\mathrm{VSV}} = 0$ at $\mathrm{FBG} = 0$

$H_2$: no linear association between FBG and VSV (i.e.\ $\mathrm{slope} = 0$)

\vspace{-0.5em}
\scriptsize\topsep=\dimexpr\topsep\relax plus \gluestretch\topsep\partopsep=\dimexpr\partopsep\relax plus \gluestretch\partopsep

```{r thuesen-lm-joint, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(ISwR)
data(thuesen)
thuesen <- thuesen[complete.cases(thuesen), ]
cf <- summary(lm(short.velocity ~ blood.glucose, data = thuesen))$coefficients
noquote(cbind(formatC(cf[, 1:3], format = "f", digits = 3), "Pr(>|t|)" = format.pval(cf[, 4], eps = 0.001, digits = 2)))
```

```{r joint-t-contour, fig.width=3.3, fig.height=2.4, fig.align="center", out.width="34%"}
crukdark <- "#00007E"; cruklight <- "#009CEE"

## The two t statistics of the linear model are jointly bivariate-t:
## same residual df as the model, correlation taken from vcov(fit).
fit  <- lm(short.velocity ~ blood.glucose, data = thuesen)
nu   <- df.residual(fit)                       # 21
V    <- vcov(fit)
rho  <- V[1, 2] / sqrt(V[1, 1] * V[2, 2])      # -0.923

dbivt <- function(x, y, nu, rho) {
  q <- (x^2 - 2 * rho * x * y + y^2) / (1 - rho^2)
  (1 + q / nu)^(-(nu + 2) / 2) / (2 * pi * sqrt(1 - rho^2))
}

g  <- seq(-4, 4, length.out = 220)
z  <- outer(g, g, dbivt, nu = nu, rho = rho)
lv <- quantile(z[z > 0], probs = c(0.55, 0.75, 0.88, 0.95, 0.985))

par(mar = c(2.6, 2.8, 0.5, 0.5), mgp = c(1.5, 0.45, 0))
contour(g, g, z, levels = lv, drawlabels = FALSE,
        col = crukdark, lwd = 1.6, axes = FALSE,
        xlab = "", ylab = "", asp = 1)
axis(1, at = seq(-4, 4, 2), cex.axis = 0.85, lwd = 1.1)
axis(2, at = seq(-4, 4, 2), cex.axis = 0.85, lwd = 1.1, las = 1)
mtext(expression(italic(t)[1] ~ "(intercept)"), side = 1, line = 1.5, cex = 0.85)
mtext(expression(italic(t)[2] ~ "(blood glucose)"), side = 2, line = 1.7, cex = 0.85)
box(bty = "l", lwd = 1.1)
```

\node[anchor=south, inner sep=0, font=\footnotesize\bfseries] at ([yshift=10pt]current page.south) {Bivariate Student's $t$ distribution under $\mathbfit{H}_{\mathbf{0}}^{\mathbf{global}}$ ($\nu = `r nu`$, $\rho = `r sprintf("%.2f", rho)`$)};

## The max-$t$ statistical principle {.t}

\vspace{-1pt}

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Let $\mathcal{F} = \{H_1, H_2, \dots, H_n\}$ be a finite family of null hypotheses

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Let $\mathcal{D}$ be the joint distribution of the individual test statistics $t_1, t_2, \dots, t_n$ under $H_0^{\mathrm{global}}$ (i.e.\ all hypotheses are \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE}). As in our example, the tests are two-sided: larger values of $|t_i|$ favour the rejection of $H_i$

\setlength{\abovedisplayskip}{2pt}\setlength{\belowdisplayskip}{2pt}$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Consider the maximum of the individual test statistics $t_i$:
$$T_{\max} = \max_{i=1, 2, \dots, n} |t_i| \qquad (\text{one-sided tests: } T_{\max} = \max\nolimits_{i} t_i)$$

\vspace{-\parskip}
\begingroup\leftskip=9pt
The joint distribution $\mathcal{D}$ determines the distribution of $T_{\max}$ under $H_0^{\mathrm{global}}$:\par
\endgroup

\vspace{-2.72em}

```{r maxt-distribution, fig.width=6.4, fig.height=1.92, fig.align="center", out.width="100%"}
crukdark <- "#00007E"; crukpink <- "#FF0087"

## T_max = max(|t_1|, |t_2|) for the two statistics of the PREVIOUS slide:
## a bivariate t with nu = 21 df and correlation rho = -0.92. The objects
## fit, nu and rho are carried over from the joint-t-contour chunk.
tobs <- summary(fit)$coefficients[, 3]
nmax <- length(tobs)
r2   <- sqrt(1 - rho^2)

## G(a) = P(|Z_1| <= a, |Z_2| <= a) on a grid, then F_max(x) = E_S[G(xS)]
## with S = sqrt(chi^2_nu / nu) independent of (Z_1, Z_2).
ag <- seq(0, 16, length.out = 700)
zg <- seq(-9, 9, length.out = 801); dz <- diff(zg)[1]
Gg <- vapply(ag, function(a) {
  z <- zg[abs(zg) <= a]
  if (!length(z)) return(0)
  sum(dnorm(z) * (pnorm((a - rho * z) / r2) -
                  pnorm((-a - rho * z) / r2))) * dz
}, numeric(1))

sg <- seq(0.25, 2.8, length.out = 500)
ws <- 2 * nu * sg * dchisq(nu * sg^2, df = nu) * diff(sg)[1]
Fmax <- function(x) sum(ws * approx(ag, Gg, xout = x * sg, rule = 2)$y)

qcrit <- uniroot(function(x) Fmax(x) - 0.95, c(0.5, 6))$root
xlim  <- c(0, 5.2)
xs    <- seq(xlim[1], xlim[2], length.out = 420)
Fsp   <- splinefun(xs, vapply(xs, Fmax, numeric(1)))
fmax  <- function(x) Fsp(x, deriv = 1)
ys    <- fmax(xs)

par(mar = c(3.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5), mgp = c(1.5, 0.45, 0))
plot(NULL, xlim = xlim, ylim = c(0, max(ys) * 2.10),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")

## the 5% rejection region in the upper tail
xr <- seq(qcrit, xlim[2], length.out = 300)
polygon(c(xr, rev(xr)), c(fmax(xr), rep(0, length(xr))),
        col = crukpink, border = NA)

lines(xs, ys, col = crukdark, lwd = 2)

axis(1, at = 0:5, cex.axis = 1.02, lwd = 1.1)
mtext(expression(T[max]), side = 1, line = 2.0, cex = 1.2)

yq <- fmax(qcrit)
segments(qcrit, 0, qcrit, yq, col = crukpink, lwd = 1.4)
text(qcrit - 0.26, fmax(qcrit - 0.26) + max(ys) * 0.42,
     bquote(q[alpha] == .(sprintf("%.2f", qcrit))),
     col = crukpink, cex = 1.0, adj = c(0.5, 0.5))
text(qcrit + 0.72, yq + max(ys) * 0.42, "5%", col = crukpink,
     cex = 0.92, adj = c(0.5, 0.5))

## pink "Critical region" box, sized to its text
lab <- "Critical region"; lcex <- 0.92
bx <- 3.9; by <- max(ys) * 0.62
bw <- strwidth(lab, cex = lcex) * 1.22
bh <- strheight(lab, cex = lcex) * 1.5
rect(bx - bw/2, by - bh, bx + bw/2, by + bh,
     border = crukpink, lwd = 1.4, col = "white")
text(bx, by, lab, col = crukpink, cex = lcex, font = 2)
arrows(bx - bw/2 * 0.35, by - bh, qcrit + 0.35, 0.012, length = 0.05,
       lwd = 1.2, col = crukpink)

text(2.1, max(ys) * 1.507,
     substitute("Distribution of" ~ T[max] ~ "(" * n == N * "," ~ nu == NU *
                "," ~ rho == RHO * ")",
                list(N = nmax, NU = nu, RHO = sprintf("%.2f", rho))),
     col = crukdark, cex = 1.03)
```

\vspace{-0.75em}

\begingroup\scriptsize\textcolor{gray}{Data: \texttt{thuesen} dataset (\texttt{ISwR} package v`r packageDescription("ISwR")$Version`, R `r paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = ".")`)}\par\endgroup

\vspace{-1pt}

\vspace{\dimexpr-0.4em-9pt\relax}

\vspace{-0.7em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ $H_1$ is \textbf{rejected}: $|t_1| = 9.34 > q_\alpha = 2.23$, adjusted $\tilde{p}_1 < 0.001$\newline
$H_2$ is \textbf{not rejected}: $|t_2| = 2.10 < q_\alpha = 2.23$, adjusted $\tilde{p}_2 = 0.064 > 0.05$\newline
\begingroup\small (single-step max-$t$: adjusted $\tilde{p}_2 = 0.064$; step-down max-$t$: adjusted $\tilde{p}_2 = 0.048$)\par\endgroup

\vspace{1pt}

\small \textbf{Subset pivotality condition}: take \textbf{any} subset $K$ of the hypotheses. Their statistics $\{t_i : i \in K\}$ must behave the same way when only the hypotheses in $K$ are \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE} as they do when \textbf{all} of them are \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE}\normalsize

\vspace{\dimexpr-0.4em+5.5pt\relax}

\begingroup\centering\small\textbf{Under the subset pivotality condition, the FWER is controlled ($\mathrm{FWER} \leq \alpha$)}\par\endgroup

## \fontsize{14.5}{17}\selectfont How to apply the max-$t$ principle for multiple comparisons {.t}

\vspace{-2pt}

```{r maxt-recipe, fig.width=6.9, fig.height=3.55, fig.align="center", out.width="100%"}
crukdark <- "#00007E"; cruklight <- "#009CEE"; crukpink <- "#FF0087"

par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 100), ylim = c(0, 100), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
     xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")

ycen <- c(87, 63, 39, 14)            # the four rows
titles <- c("Statistical model", "Hypotheses",
            "Test statistics and their joint law",
            "How the joint law is used")
subs <- list(
  "what the data look like, and what is assumed",
  "one per comparison, all tested together",
  expression("each " * italic(t)[i] * ", and " * italic(D) * " = their joint law under " * H[0]^global),
  expression(bold("jointly") * "  or  " * bold("marginally") * " (as if uncorrelated)"))

## ---- left column: the numbered steps -------------------------------------
for (i in 1:4) {
  yc <- ycen[i]
  points(4.2, yc + 2.6, pch = 16, cex = 2.9, col = crukdark)
  text(4.2, yc + 2.6, i, col = "white", cex = 0.95, font = 2)
  text(10, yc + 2.6, titles[i], col = crukdark, cex = 1.15, font = 2, adj = c(0, 0.5))
  text(10, yc - 4.8, subs[[i]], col = "grey30", cex = 0.95, adj = c(0, 0.5))
}

## ---- right column: one small picture per step ----------------------------
bx <- 60; bw <- 38                   # drawing band

## 1. three groups, drawn as densities on a baseline
y1 <- ycen[1]
segments(bx, y1 - 7, bx + bw, y1 - 7, col = "grey45", lwd = 1)
for (k in 0:2) {
  mu <- bx + 7 + k * 11
  xx <- seq(mu - 5, mu + 5, length.out = 60)
  yy <- (y1 - 7) + 13 * dnorm(xx, mu, 2.1) / dnorm(0, 0, 2.1)
  polygon(c(xx, rev(xx)), c(yy, rep(y1 - 7, length(xx))),
          col = adjustcolor(cruklight, 0.18), border = NA)
  lines(xx, yy, col = if (k == 0) crukpink else cruklight, lwd = 1.8)
}
text(bx + bw/2, y1 - 11, "groups", col = "grey35", cex = 0.72)

## 2. one hypothesis per comparison
y2 <- ycen[2]
for (k in 0:2) {
  xx <- bx + 1 + k * 13
  rect(xx, y2 - 3.6, xx + 11, y2 + 4.4, border = crukdark, lwd = 1.2, col = "white")
  text(xx + 5.5, y2 + 0.4,
       c(expression(H[1]), expression(H[2]), expression(H[n]))[[k + 1]],
       col = crukdark, cex = 0.82)
}
text(bx + 19.5, y2 - 7.5, "tested as one family", col = "grey35", cex = 0.72)

## 3. the statistics, and D as their joint cloud
y3 <- ycen[3]
set.seed(4)
for (k in 0:2) {
  xx <- bx + 2 + k * 6
  text(xx, y3 + 4.5, c(expression(t[1]), expression(t[2]), expression(t[n]))[[k + 1]],
       col = crukdark, cex = 0.82)
}
arrows(bx + 16, y3 + 4.5, bx + 21, y3 + 4.5, length = 0.05, lwd = 1.2, col = crukdark)
## a tilted cloud = D
cx <- bx + 30; cy <- y3 + 1
th <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 120)
for (rr in c(1, 1.9)) {
  ex <- rr * 5.2 * cos(th); ey <- rr * 2.6 * sin(th)
  a  <- pi / 4
  lines(cx + ex * cos(a) - ey * sin(a), cy + ex * sin(a) + ey * cos(a),
        col = cruklight, lwd = 1.5)
}
text(cx, y3 - 8.5, expression(italic(D)), col = crukdark, cex = 1.0, font = 2)

## 4. joint versus marginal, side by side
y4 <- ycen[4]
## -- joint: the cloud with one max-t cut
jx <- bx + 7
for (rr in c(1, 1.8)) {
  ex <- rr * 4.2 * cos(th); ey <- rr * 2.1 * sin(th)
  a  <- pi / 4
  lines(jx + ex * cos(a) - ey * sin(a), y4 + ex * sin(a) + ey * cos(a),
        col = cruklight, lwd = 1.3)
}
rect(jx - 8.2, y4 - 8.2, jx + 8.2, y4 + 8.2, border = crukpink, lwd = 1.5, lty = 1)
text(jx, y4 - 11.5, "jointly", col = crukpink, cex = 0.78, font = 2)
## -- marginal: two separate axes, each cut on its own
mx <- bx + 29
for (k in 0:1) {
  yy <- y4 + 4.5 - k * 9
  segments(mx - 9, yy, mx + 9, yy, col = "grey45", lwd = 1)
  xx <- seq(mx - 9, mx + 9, length.out = 60)
  lines(xx, yy + 6 * dnorm(xx, mx, 3.4) / dnorm(0, 0, 3.4), col = cruklight, lwd = 1.3)
  segments(mx + c(-5.6, 5.6), yy, mx + c(-5.6, 5.6), yy + 5, col = crukpink, lwd = 1.4)
}
text(mx, y4 - 11.5, "marginally", col = crukpink, cex = 0.78, font = 2)
```

\vspace{-0.7em}

\begingroup\centering\footnotesize\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{Jointly}}: critical value(s) from $\mathcal{D}$, correlations used. \textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{Marginally}}: each one alone, as if uncorrelated\par\endgroup

## Dunnett's test {.t}

\vspace{-1pt}

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Statistical model}: one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA)

\vspace{-1.2em}

```{r dunnett-anova, fig.width=6.8, fig.height=1.60, fig.align="center", out.width="92%"}
crukdark <- "#00007E"; cruklight <- "#009CEE"; crukpink <- "#FF0087"

sig <- 0.55
mus <- c(0, 2.6, 4.4, 7.4)
labs <- list(expression("Control " * mu[0]), expression("Arm 1 " * mu[1]),
             expression("Arm 2 " * mu[2]), expression("Arm " * italic(n) * " " * mu[italic(n)]))
cols <- c(crukpink, cruklight, cruklight, cruklight)

par(mar = c(1.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.3))
plot(NULL, xlim = c(-1.6, 14.6), ylim = c(0, dnorm(0, 0, sig) * 1.42),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
segments(-1.6, 0, max(mus) + 3.2 * sig, 0, col = "grey40", lwd = 1)
for (k in seq_along(mus)) {
  xs <- seq(mus[k] - 3.2 * sig, mus[k] + 3.2 * sig, length.out = 300)
  polygon(c(xs, rev(xs)), c(dnorm(xs, mus[k], sig), rep(0, length(xs))),
          col = adjustcolor(cols[k], 0.18), border = NA)
  lines(xs, dnorm(xs, mus[k], sig), col = cols[k], lwd = 2)
  segments(mus[k], 0, mus[k], dnorm(mus[k], mus[k], sig), col = cols[k], lty = 2, lwd = 1)
  mtext(labs[[k]], side = 1, line = 0.25, at = mus[k], cex = 0.78, col = cols[k])
}
text(5.9, 0.12, expression(cdots), cex = 1.4, col = crukdark)

## the two assumptions, in boxes on the right
## equal-height boxes, in one row across the top of the plot region
box_row <- function(txts, cx = 0.78, off = integer(0)) {
  ## one row of boxes across the top, identical on every slide.
  ## `off` marks the assumptions this test does NOT need: those boxes are
  ## greyed and struck through with a red cross.
  repeat {
    ws  <- sapply(txts, strwidth, cex = cx) * 1.06
    gap <- strwidth("n", cex = cx) * 2.0
    tot <- sum(ws) + gap * (length(txts) - 1)
    if (tot <= diff(par("usr")[1:2]) * 0.995 || cx < 0.45) break
    cx <- cx * 0.96
  }
  bh <- max(sapply(txts, strheight, cex = cx)) * 1.7
  y  <- par("usr")[4] - bh / 2
  x0 <- par("usr")[2] - tot
  par(xpd = NA)
  for (i in seq_along(txts)) {
    xl   <- x0 + sum(ws[seq_len(i - 1)]) + gap * (i - 1)
    dead <- i %in% off
    rect(xl, y - bh/2, xl + ws[i], y + bh/2,
         border = if (dead) "grey60" else crukdark, lwd = 1.3, col = "white")
    text(xl + ws[i]/2, y, txts[[i]], cex = cx,
         col = if (dead) "grey55" else crukdark, font = 2)
    if (dead) {
      segments(xl, y - bh/2, xl + ws[i], y + bh/2, col = crukpink, lwd = 1.8)
      segments(xl, y + bh/2, xl + ws[i], y - bh/2, col = crukpink, lwd = 1.8)
    }
  }
}
box_row(list(
  expression(bold("Normality: ") * Y[ki] %~% N(mu[k], sigma^2)),
  expression(bold("Equal variances: ") * "same " * sigma^2),
  expression(bold("Independence: ") * Y[ki] * " independent")))
```

\vspace{-1.3em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Hypotheses}: }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Hypotheses}: $H_k : \mu_k = \mu_0$, $k = 1, \dots, n$\vspace{3.5pt}\newline {\fontsize{10.5pt}{12.5pt}\selectfont For each of the $n$ arms, the arm mean equals the control mean $\mu_0$\par}

\vspace{0.25em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Each $t_k$ follows a Student's $t$ distribution with $N - (n+1)$ degrees of freedom under $H_k$ \mbox{\footnotesize($N$ = total sample size)}\newline
\colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}$\mathcal{D}$} is a multivariate Student's $t$ distribution under $H_0^{\mathrm{global}}$

\vspace{-1pt}

\noindent\hspace*{14.5pt}\tikz[baseline=-0.55ex, overlay]{\draw[-{Latex[length=5pt,width=4pt]}, thick, crukdark] (0,9.5pt) -- (0,0) -- (16pt,0);}\hspace{20pt}\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{The max-$t$ principle is applied to $\mathcal{D}$}}\par

## Tukey's test {.t}

\vspace{-1pt}

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Statistical model}: one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA)

\vspace{-1.2em}

```{r tukey-anova, fig.width=6.8, fig.height=1.60, fig.align="center", out.width="92%"}
crukdark <- "#00007E"; cruklight <- "#009CEE"; crukpink <- "#FF0087"

sig <- 0.55
mus <- c(0, 2.8, 5.3, 8.3)

             expression("Group 3 " * mu[3]), expression("Group " * italic(k) * " " * mu[italic(k)]))
cols <- c(cruklight, cruklight, cruklight, cruklight)

par(mar = c(1.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.3))
plot(NULL, xlim = c(-1.6, 15.6), ylim = c(0, dnorm(0, 0, sig) * 1.42),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
segments(-1.6, 0, max(mus) + 3.2 * sig, 0, col = "grey40", lwd = 1)
for (k in seq_along(mus)) {
  xs <- seq(mus[k] - 3.2 * sig, mus[k] + 3.2 * sig, length.out = 300)
  polygon(c(xs, rev(xs)), c(dnorm(xs, mus[k], sig), rep(0, length(xs))),
          col = adjustcolor(cols[k], 0.18), border = NA)
  lines(xs, dnorm(xs, mus[k], sig), col = cols[k], lwd = 2)
  segments(mus[k], 0, mus[k], dnorm(mus[k], mus[k], sig), col = cols[k], lty = 2, lwd = 1)
  mtext(labs[[k]], side = 1, line = 0.25, at = mus[k], cex = 0.78, col = cols[k])
}
text(6.8, 0.12, expression(cdots), cex = 1.4, col = crukdark)

## the two assumptions, in boxes on the right
## equal-height boxes, in one row across the top of the plot region
box_row <- function(txts, cx = 0.78, off = integer(0)) {
  ## one row of boxes across the top, identical on every slide.
  ## `off` marks the assumptions this test does NOT need: those boxes are
  ## greyed and struck through with a red cross.
  repeat {
    ws  <- sapply(txts, strwidth, cex = cx) * 1.06
    gap <- strwidth("n", cex = cx) * 2.0
    tot <- sum(ws) + gap * (length(txts) - 1)
    if (tot <= diff(par("usr")[1:2]) * 0.995 || cx < 0.45) break
    cx <- cx * 0.96
  }
  bh <- max(sapply(txts, strheight, cex = cx)) * 1.7
  y  <- par("usr")[4] - bh / 2
  x0 <- par("usr")[2] - tot
  par(xpd = NA)
  for (i in seq_along(txts)) {
    xl   <- x0 + sum(ws[seq_len(i - 1)]) + gap * (i - 1)
    dead <- i %in% off
    rect(xl, y - bh/2, xl + ws[i], y + bh/2,
         border = if (dead) "grey60" else crukdark, lwd = 1.3, col = "white")
    text(xl + ws[i]/2, y, txts[[i]], cex = cx,
         col = if (dead) "grey55" else crukdark, font = 2)
    if (dead) {
      segments(xl, y - bh/2, xl + ws[i], y + bh/2, col = crukpink, lwd = 1.8)
      segments(xl, y + bh/2, xl + ws[i], y - bh/2, col = crukpink, lwd = 1.8)
    }
  }
}
box_row(list(
  expression(bold("Normality: ") * Y[ji] %~% N(mu[j], sigma^2)),
  expression(bold("Equal variances: ") * "same " * sigma^2),
  expression(bold("Independence: ") * Y[ji] * " independent")))
```

\vspace{-1.3em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Hypotheses}: }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Hypotheses}: $H_{j\ell} : \mu_j = \mu_\ell$, $1 \leq j < \ell \leq k$\vspace{1.5pt}\newline {\fontsize{10.5pt}{12.5pt}\selectfont For each of the $n = k(k-1)/2$ pairs, the two group means are equal\par}

\vspace{0.25em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Each $t_{j\ell}$ follows a Student's $t$ distribution with $N - k$ degrees of freedom under $H_{j\ell}$\newline
\colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}$\mathcal{D}$} is a multivariate Student's $t$ distribution under $H_0^{\mathrm{global}}$

\vspace{-1pt}

\noindent\hspace*{14.5pt}\tikz[baseline=-0.55ex, overlay]{\draw[-{Latex[length=5pt,width=4pt]}, thick, crukdark] (0,9.5pt) -- (0,0) -- (16pt,0);}\hspace{20pt}\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{The max-$t$ principle is applied to $\mathcal{D}$}}\par


## \fontsize{15.5}{18}\selectfont Dunnett's test with unequal variances (Hasler--Hothorn) {.t}

\vspace{-1pt}

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Statistical model}: one-way ANOVA \textbf{without} the equal-variance assumption

\vspace{-1.2em}

```{r dunnett-unequalvar, fig.width=6.8, fig.height=1.60, fig.align="center", out.width="92%"}
crukdark <- "#00007E"; cruklight <- "#009CEE"; crukpink <- "#FF0087"

sigs <- c(0.40, 0.78, 0.50, 0.92)
mus  <- c(0, 2.6, 4.4, 7.4)
labs <- list(expression("Control " * mu[0]), expression("Arm 1 " * mu[1]),
             expression("Arm 2 " * mu[2]), expression("Arm " * italic(n) * " " * mu[italic(n)]))
cols <- c(crukpink, cruklight, cruklight, cruklight)

par(mar = c(1.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.3))
plot(NULL, xlim = c(-1.6, 14.6), ylim = c(0, dnorm(0, 0, min(sigs)) * 1.42),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
segments(-1.6, 0, max(mus + 3.2 * sigs), 0, col = "grey40", lwd = 1)
for (k in seq_along(mus)) {
  xs <- seq(mus[k] - 3.2 * sigs[k], mus[k] + 3.2 * sigs[k], length.out = 300)
  polygon(c(xs, rev(xs)), c(dnorm(xs, mus[k], sigs[k]), rep(0, length(xs))),
          col = adjustcolor(cols[k], 0.18), border = NA)
  lines(xs, dnorm(xs, mus[k], sigs[k]), col = cols[k], lwd = 2)
  segments(mus[k], 0, mus[k], dnorm(mus[k], mus[k], sigs[k]), col = cols[k], lty = 2, lwd = 1)
  mtext(labs[[k]], side = 1, line = 0.25, at = mus[k], cex = 0.78, col = cols[k])
}
text(5.9, dnorm(0, 0, min(sigs)) * 0.25, expression(cdots), cex = 1.4, col = crukdark)

box_row <- function(txts, cx = 0.78, off = integer(0)) {
  ## one row of boxes across the top, identical on every slide.
  ## `off` marks the assumptions this test does NOT need: those boxes are
  ## greyed and struck through with a red cross.
  repeat {
    ws  <- sapply(txts, strwidth, cex = cx) * 1.06
    gap <- strwidth("n", cex = cx) * 2.0
    tot <- sum(ws) + gap * (length(txts) - 1)
    if (tot <= diff(par("usr")[1:2]) * 0.995 || cx < 0.45) break
    cx <- cx * 0.96
  }
  bh <- max(sapply(txts, strheight, cex = cx)) * 1.7
  y  <- par("usr")[4] - bh / 2
  x0 <- par("usr")[2] - tot
  par(xpd = NA)
  for (i in seq_along(txts)) {
    xl   <- x0 + sum(ws[seq_len(i - 1)]) + gap * (i - 1)
    dead <- i %in% off
    rect(xl, y - bh/2, xl + ws[i], y + bh/2,
         border = if (dead) "grey60" else crukdark, lwd = 1.3, col = "white")
    text(xl + ws[i]/2, y, txts[[i]], cex = cx,
         col = if (dead) "grey55" else crukdark, font = 2)
    if (dead) {
      segments(xl, y - bh/2, xl + ws[i], y + bh/2, col = crukpink, lwd = 1.8)
      segments(xl, y + bh/2, xl + ws[i], y - bh/2, col = crukpink, lwd = 1.8)
    }
  }
}

box_row(list(
  expression(bold("Normality: ") * Y[ki] %~% N(mu[k], sigma[k]^2)),
  expression(bold("Equal variances: ") * "same " * sigma^2),
  expression(bold("Independence: ") * Y[ki] * " independent")), off = 2)
```

\vspace{-1.3em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Hypotheses}: }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Hypotheses}: $H_k : \mu_k = \mu_0$, $k = 1, \dots, n$\vspace{3.5pt}\newline {\fontsize{10.5pt}{12.5pt}\selectfont For each of the $n$ arms, the arm mean equals the control mean $\mu_0$\par}

\vspace{0.25em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Each $t_k$ (Welch) follows \textbf{approximately} a Student's $t$ distribution under $H_k$\newline
\colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}$\mathcal{D}$} is \textbf{approximately} a multivariate Student's $t$ under $H_0^{\mathrm{global}}$ \mbox{\footnotesize(Satterthwaite df, \textbf{estimated} correlations; needs \textbf{moderate} $n_k$)}

\vspace{-1pt}

\noindent\hspace*{14.5pt}\tikz[baseline=-0.55ex, overlay]{\draw[-{Latex[length=5pt,width=4pt]}, thick, crukdark] (0,9.5pt) -- (0,0) -- (16pt,0);}\hspace{20pt}\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{The max-$t$ principle is applied to $\mathcal{D}$}}\par

\vfill

## \fontsize{15.5}{18}\selectfont Dunnett-type test without normality (Steel) {.t}

\vspace{-1pt}

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Statistical model}: one-way layout \textbf{without} the normality assumption

\vspace{-1.2em}

```{r steel-nonormal, fig.width=6.8, fig.height=1.60, fig.align="center", out.width="92%"}
crukdark <- "#00007E"; cruklight <- "#009CEE"; crukpink <- "#FF0087"

## one skewed, non-normal shape shifted in location: under each pair's null the
## two compared groups share one distribution, as the middle box says
sh <- rep(2.6, 4); sc <- rep(0.55, 4)
mus  <- c(0, 2.6, 5.0, 7.8)
labs <- list(expression("Control " * F[0]), expression("Arm 1 " * F[1]),
             expression("Arm 2 " * F[2]), expression("Arm " * italic(n) * " " * F[italic(n)]))
cols <- c(crukpink, cruklight, cruklight, cruklight)
ytop <- max(dgamma((sh - 1) * sc, shape = sh, scale = sc))

par(mar = c(1.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.3))
plot(NULL, xlim = c(-1.6, 14.6), ylim = c(0, ytop * 1.42),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
segments(-1.6, 0, max(mus + qgamma(0.995, shape = sh, scale = sc)), 0,
         col = "grey40", lwd = 1)
for (k in seq_along(mus)) {
  xs <- seq(mus[k], mus[k] + qgamma(0.995, shape = sh[k], scale = sc[k]), length.out = 300)
  ds <- dgamma(xs - mus[k], shape = sh[k], scale = sc[k])
  polygon(c(xs, rev(xs)), c(ds, rep(0, length(xs))),
          col = adjustcolor(cols[k], 0.18), border = NA)
  lines(xs, ds, col = cols[k], lwd = 2)
  mtext(labs[[k]], side = 1, line = 0.25, at = mus[k] + (sh[k] - 1) * sc[k],
        cex = 0.78, col = cols[k])
}
## the gammas overlap, so the ellipsis goes in the flattest gap, clear of every curve
text(7.92, ytop * 0.30, expression(cdots), cex = 1.4, col = crukdark)

box_row(list(
```

\vspace{-1.3em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Hypotheses}: }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Hypotheses}: $H_k : F_k = F_0$, $k = 1, \dots, n$\vspace{3.5pt}\newline {\fontsize{10.5pt}{12.5pt}\selectfont For each of the $n$ arms, the arm distribution equals the control distribution $F_0$\par}

\vspace{0.25em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Each $t_k$ (standardised Wilcoxon rank sum, \textbf{ranked within the control--arm pair only}) is \textbf{asymptotically} standard normal under $H_k$ \mbox{\footnotesize(no ties)}\newline
\colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}$\mathcal{D}$} is \textbf{asymptotically} a multivariate normal distribution under $H_0^{\mathrm{global}}$
