## \fontsize{14.5}{17}\selectfont How to apply non-max-$t$ procedures for multiple comparisons {.t}

\vspace{2pt}

```{r nomaxt-recipe, fig.width=6.9, fig.height=3.45, fig.align="center", out.width="100%"}
crukdark <- "#00007E"; cruklight <- "#009CEE"; crukpink  <- "#FF0087"

par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 100), ylim = c(0, 100), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
     xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")

ycen <- c(82, 50, 18)
titles <- c("Joint distribution", "Test by hypothesis", "Correction")
subs <- list(
  expression("same start as max-" * italic(t) * ": " * italic(D) * ", but only its margins"),
  expression("one test each, from its own margin of " * italic(D)),
  expression("Bonferroni or Holm on the raw " * italic(p) * "-values"))

for (i in 1:3) {
  yc <- ycen[i]
  points(4.2, yc + 3, pch = 16, cex = 2.9, col = crukdark)
  text(4.2, yc + 3, i, col = "white", cex = 0.95, font = 2)
  text(10, yc + 3, titles[i], col = crukdark, cex = 1.15, font = 2, adj = c(0, 0.5))
  text(10, yc - 5, subs[[i]], col = "grey30", cex = 0.95, adj = c(0, 0.5))
}

bx <- 58
th <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 120)
ell <- function(cx, cy, rx, ry, col, lwd) {
  a1 <- pi / 4
  for (rr in c(1, 1.9)) {
    ex <- rr * rx * cos(th); ey <- rr * ry * sin(th)
    lines(cx + ex * cos(a1) - ey * sin(a1), cy + ex * sin(a1) + ey * cos(a1),
          col = col, lwd = lwd)
  }
}

## 1. the same joint law as on the max-t slide; only its margins are used
y1 <- ycen[1]; cx <- bx + 18; cy <- y1 + 1
ell(cx, cy, 5.6, 2.8, cruklight, 1.5)
text(cx, y1 - 12, expression(italic(D)), col = crukdark, cex = 1.0, font = 2)

## 2. one p-value per hypothesis, each from its own margin of D
y2 <- ycen[2]
hl <- list(expression(H[1]), expression(H[2]), expression(H[n]))
pl <- list(expression(italic(p)[1]), expression(italic(p)[2]), expression(italic(p)[n]))
for (k in 0:2) {
  yy <- y2 + 8 - k * 8
  rect(bx - 1, yy - 3, bx + 9, yy + 3, border = crukdark, lwd = 1.1, col = "white")
  text(bx + 4, yy, hl[[k + 1]], col = crukdark, cex = 0.78)
  arrows(bx + 10.5, yy, bx + 15.5, yy, length = 0.04, lwd = 1.1, col = "grey45")
  text(bx + 18.5, yy, pl[[k + 1]], col = crukdark, cex = 0.78)
}
## 3. the raw p-values against one shared threshold
y3 <- ycen[3]; px <- bx + 6
for (k in 0:2) {
  yy <- y3 + 8 - k * 8
  text(px, yy, pl[[k + 1]], col = crukdark, cex = 0.78)
  segments(px + 4, yy, px + 4 + c(17, 4, 13)[k + 1], yy, col = cruklight, lwd = 3.4)
}
segments(px + 10, y3 - 11, px + 10, y3 + 13, col = crukpink, lwd = 1.7, lty = 2)
text(px + 10, y3 - 14, expression(alpha / italic(n)), col = crukpink, cex = 0.86)
```

\vspace{-0.4em}

\begingroup\centering\footnotesize One test per hypothesis from its \textbf{margin} of $\mathcal{D}$, then multiplicity by \textbf{correcting the $p$-values}\par\endgroup

## Dunn's test (not a max-$t$ procedure) {.t}

\vspace{-1pt}

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Statistical model}: one-way layout \textbf{without} normality, all $k$ groups \textbf{alike}

\vspace{-1.2em}

```{r dunn-nonormal, fig.width=6.8, fig.height=1.60, fig.align="center", out.width="92%"}
crukdark <- "#00007E"; cruklight <- "#009CEE"; crukpink <- "#FF0087"

## Dunn assumes every group has the SAME distribution, so the k curves coincide:
## they are drawn with a hair of offset only so that several are visible
sh <- 2.6; sc <- 0.55
mus  <- 5.4 + c(0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15)
ytop <- dgamma((sh - 1) * sc, shape = sh, scale = sc)

par(mar = c(1.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.3))
plot(NULL, xlim = c(-1.6, 15.6), ylim = c(0, ytop * 1.42),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
segments(-1.6, 0, max(mus) + 4.6, 0, col = "grey40", lwd = 1)
for (k in seq_along(mus)) {
  xs <- seq(mus[k], mus[k] + 4.4, length.out = 300)
  ds <- dgamma(xs - mus[k], shape = sh, scale = sc)
  if (k == 1)
    polygon(c(xs, rev(xs)), c(ds, rep(0, length(xs))),
            col = adjustcolor(cruklight, 0.18), border = NA)
  lines(xs, ds, col = cruklight, lwd = 2)
}
mtext(expression(F[1] ~ "=" ~ F[2] ~ "=" ~ F[3] ~ "=" ~ F[italic(k)]), side = 1, line = 0.25,
      at = mus[1] + (sh - 1) * sc + 0.2, cex = 0.82, col = cruklight)


box_row <- function(txts, cx = 0.78, off = integer(0)) {
  ## one row of boxes across the top, identical on every slide.
  ## `off` marks the assumptions this test does NOT need: those boxes are
  ## greyed and struck through with a red cross.
  repeat {
    ws  <- sapply(txts, strwidth, cex = cx) * 1.06
    gap <- strwidth("n", cex = cx) * 2.0
    tot <- sum(ws) + gap * (length(txts) - 1)
    if (tot <= diff(par("usr")[1:2]) * 0.995 || cx < 0.45) break
    cx <- cx * 0.96
  }
  bh <- max(sapply(txts, strheight, cex = cx)) * 1.7
  y  <- par("usr")[4] - bh / 2
  x0 <- par("usr")[2] - tot
  par(xpd = NA)
  for (i in seq_along(txts)) {
    xl   <- x0 + sum(ws[seq_len(i - 1)]) + gap * (i - 1)
    dead <- i %in% off
    rect(xl, y - bh/2, xl + ws[i], y + bh/2,
         border = if (dead) "grey60" else crukdark, lwd = 1.3, col = "white")
    text(xl + ws[i]/2, y, txts[[i]], cex = cx,
         col = if (dead) "grey55" else crukdark, font = 2)
    if (dead) {
      segments(xl, y - bh/2, xl + ws[i], y + bh/2, col = crukpink, lwd = 1.8)
      segments(xl, y + bh/2, xl + ws[i], y - bh/2, col = crukpink, lwd = 1.8)
    }
  }
}

box_row(list(
  expression(bold("Normality: ") * Y[ji] %~% N(mu[j], sigma^2)),
  expression(bold("Same distribution: ") * "all " * italic(k) * " groups"),
  expression(bold("Independence: ") * Y[ji] * " independent")), off = 1)
```

\vspace{-1.3em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Hypotheses}: }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Hypotheses}: $H_{j\ell} : F_j = F_\ell$, $1 \leq j < \ell \leq k$\vspace{1.5pt}\newline {\fontsize{10.5pt}{12.5pt}\selectfont For each of the $n = k(k-1)/2$ pairs, the two group distributions are equal\par}

\vspace{0.25em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textbf{Test statistic} for each pair, from the \textbf{mean ranks} $\bar{R}_j$ over all $N$ observations, standardised under $H_0^{\mathrm{global}}$ \mbox{\footnotesize(no ties)}: a \textbf{$p$-value for each pair}\par

\vspace{0.25em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textbf{Bonferroni} or \textbf{Holm} is then applied to these $n$ $p$-values: only the \textbf{margins} of $\mathcal{D}$ are used\par

\vfill

\begingroup\footnotesize\noindent\setlength{\fboxsep}{3.5pt}\fcolorbox{crukpink}{white}{\parbox{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\fboxsep-2\fboxrule\relax}{\centerline{Dunn assumes \textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{all $k$ groups have the same distribution}}; otherwise \textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{FWER}} can \textbf{far exceed} $\alpha$}}}\par\endgroup

## FWER and statistical power: the Achilles' heel {.t}

\vspace{-0.05em}

For each gene, expression was simulated in a control and a treatment group ($5$ units each), drawn from a normal distribution ($\mu = 0$, $\sigma = 1$). For a fraction of genes (10\% and 50\%), an effect size $\mathrm{ES} = 2$ ($\sim$ 79\% power, $\alpha = 0.05$) was simulated by setting $\mu = 2$ in the treatment sample

\vspace{-0.6em}

\begin{center}
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth,height=0.53\textheight,keepaspectratio]{FWER and statistical power.png}
\end{center}

\vspace{-1.0em}

Genes were assumed to be statistically independent.

## FWER and statistical power: the Achilles' heel {.t}

\vspace{-0.05em}

\begingroup\centering
\textbf{\% of truly differentially expressed genes declared significant}\par
\endgroup

\vspace{-1.1em}

```{r fwer-power-table, results="asis"}
## Results come from the cached, seeded simulation in fwer-power-simulation.R;
## the script re-runs only if the CSV is missing.
if (!file.exists("fwer-power-simulation.csv")) source("fwer-power-simulation.R")
pw <- read.csv("fwer-power-simulation.csv", check.names = FALSE)

fmt <- function(x) formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = 2)

cat("\\begin{center}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{r|ccc|ccc}\n\\hline\n")
cat("& \\multicolumn{3}{c|}{\\textcolor{crukdark}{10\\% affected}}",
    "& \\multicolumn{3}{c}{\\textcolor{crukdark}{50\\% affected}} \\\\\n")
cat("$n$ & Bonf. & Holm & \\v{S}id\\'ak &",
    "Bonf. & Holm & \\v{S}id\\'ak \\\\\n\\hline\n")
for (N in sort(unique(pw$N))) {
  a <- pw[pw$N == N & pw$frac == 0.1, ]
  b <- pw[pw$N == N & pw$frac == 0.5, ]
  cat(formatC(N, format = "d", big.mark = ","), "&",
      paste(fmt(c(a$Bonferroni, a$Holm, a$Sidak,
                  b$Bonferroni, b$Holm, b$Sidak)), collapse = " & "),
      "\\\\\n")
}
cat("\\hline\n\\end{tabular}\\par\\vspace{3pt}\n{\\footnotesize Legend: $n$ = number of genes; Bonf.\\ = Bonferroni correction; $10^5$ simulated trials per $n$\\par}\n\\normalsize\n\\end{center}\n")
```

\vspace{0.2em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Power collapses as the family grows: with $n = 10$, about
$\textcolor{crukdark}{35\%}$ of the truly affected genes are detected; with
$n = 100{,}000$, only $\textcolor{crukdark}{0.02\%}$

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ All three corrections give essentially the same power. The
step-wise gain (Holm) is visible only for small $n$ with many true effects

## False discovery rate (FDR) {.t}

\vspace{-6pt}

Let $\mathcal{F} = \{H_1, H_2, \dots, H_n\}$ be a finite family of null hypotheses, and let $m_0$ ($0 \le m_0 \le n$) denote the number of \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE} \textbf{null hypotheses}.

\vspace{-0.4em}

\begin{center}
\normalsize
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\hline
$\mathcal{F}$ & Not Rejected & Rejected & Total \\
\hline
\colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE}  & \color{crukdark}$U$ & \colorbox{crukpink}{\color{crukdark}$V$} & $m_0$ \\
\colorbox{green}{\color{black}FALSE} & \color{crukdark}$T$ & \color{crukdark}$S$ & $n - m_0$ \\
\hline
Total & \color{crukdark}$n - R$ & \colorbox{crukpink}{\color{crukdark}$R$} & $n$ \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\begingroup
\setlength{\leftmargini}{0pt}

\hangindent=9pt\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Consider the \textbf{proportion} of rejections that are false, $\textcolor{crukdark}{Q} = \textcolor{crukdark}{V} / \textcolor{crukdark}{R}$, with the convention $\textcolor{crukdark}{Q = 0}$ when \color{crukdark}$R = 0$\color{black}

\hangindent=9pt\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ $\textcolor{crukdark}{Q}$ is a random variable that cannot be observed: \color{crukdark}$R$ \color{black} is known once the tests are run, but \color{crukdark}$V$ \color{black} is not. We therefore control its \textbf{expectation}

\endgroup

\vspace{-0.3em}

\begin{center}
\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{\large FDR $\boldsymbol{:=}$ E$\left[\,\colorbox{crukpink}{$Q$}\,\right]$}}
\end{center}

\vspace{-0.7em}

\begingroup\centering\small
We accept that, \textbf{on average}, a controlled \textbf{proportion of our discoveries is false}.\par\vspace{-\parskip}
\textbf{We tolerate some errors in exchange for more power.}\par
\endgroup

## FWER and FDR as the number of tests grows

\vspace{0.5em}

\begingroup
\setlength{\leftmargini}{0pt}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Let $\mathcal{F} = \{H_1, H_2, \dots, H_n\}$ be a finite family of null hypotheses with \textbf{independent} test statistics, each tested at level $\alpha$

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ In both series $80\%$ of the nulls are \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE} ($m_0 = 0.8\,n$, no effect); the other $20\%$ are \colorbox{green}{\color{black}FALSE}, each detected with an assumed \textbf{power} $\boldsymbol{= 90\%}$ at every $\alpha$

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l@{\hspace{2.2em}}l@{}}
$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textbf{Filled}: FWER $= 1 - (1-\alpha)^{m_0}$ &
$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textbf{Open}: FDR $= \mathrm{E}[V/R]$ \\[-0.1em]
\phantom{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textbf{Filled}: }{\small\textcolor{crukdark}{(a probability)}} &
\phantom{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textbf{Open}: }{\small\textcolor{crukdark}{(an expected proportion)}}
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{-1.9em}

\endgroup

```{r fwer-plot-2, fig.width=6.2, fig.height=2.85, fig.align="center", out.width="84%"}
n      <- 0:100
alphas <- c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001)
cols   <- c("#FF0087", "#009CEE", "#00007E")
labs   <- c(expression(alpha == 0.05), expression(alpha == 0.01),
            expression(alpha == 0.001))

## FDR = E[V/R] when a fraction of the n hypotheses are false nulls, each
## detected with probability `power`: V ~ Binomial(m0, alpha) false positives
## and S ~ Binomial(m1, power) true discoveries, R = V + S, Q = 0 when R = 0.
fdr_curve <- function(n, alpha, frac_false = 0.2, power = 0.9) {
  vapply(n, function(nn) {
    m1 <- round(frac_false * nn)
    m0 <- nn - m1
    if (m0 == 0) return(0)
    v  <- 0:m0
    s  <- 0:m1
    q  <- outer(v, s, function(V, S) ifelse(V + S == 0, 0, V / (V + S)))
    sum(outer(dbinom(v, m0, alpha), dbinom(s, m1, power)) * q)
  }, numeric(1))
}

par(mar = c(2.6, 4.6, 0.6, 9.5), mgp = c(2.2, 0.5, 0), xpd = FALSE)
plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 100), ylim = c(0, 1), bty = "n", las = 1, xaxt = "n",
     xaxs = "i", xlab = "",
     ylab = "Error rate", cex.axis = 0.9, cex.lab = 1.4)
axis(1, at = seq(0, 100, 20), cex.axis = 0.9)

abline(h = seq(0, 1, 0.25), col = "grey88", lwd = 0.8)

## one point estimate for every n = 0, 1, ..., 100, never joined up:
## m0 = n - round(0.2 n) true nulls and m1 = round(0.2 n) false nulls
m0v <- n - round(0.2 * n)
for (i in seq_along(alphas)) {
  points(n, 1 - (1 - alphas[i])^m0v, col = cols[i], pch = 19, cex = 0.34)
  points(n, fdr_curve(n, alphas[i]), col = cols[i], pch = 1, cex = 0.40,
         lwd = 0.9)
}

par(xpd = NA)
mtext(expression(italic(n)), side = 1, line = 0.5, at = 108, cex = 1.4, las = 1)

legend(x = 108, y = 0.68, legend = labs, col = cols, pch = 19, pt.cex = 1.0,
       bty = "n", cex = 1.2, text.col = "grey15",
       y.intersp = 1.5, xjust = 0, yjust = 0.5)

legend(x = 108, y = 0.13, legend = c("FWER", "FDR"), pch = c(19, 1),
       col = "grey35", pt.cex = c(0.9, 1.0), pt.lwd = 1.2, bty = "n",
       cex = 0.95, text.col = "grey15", y.intersp = 1.4, xjust = 0,
       yjust = 0.5)
```

## Three questions about the FDR {.t}

\vspace{1.2em}

\begingroup\setlength{\leftmargini}{0pt}

\Large

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textbf{How can we control the FDR?}

\vspace{1.2em}

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textbf{How can we estimate the FDR?}

\vspace{1.2em}

$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textbf{How can we compute FDR-adjusted $\boldsymbol{p}$-values?}

\normalsize

\endgroup

## Uniform distribution of the $p$-value {.t}

\vspace{-0.01em}

\begingroup
Let the null hypothesis $H_0$ be \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE}, and let the $p$-value be computed from the \textbf{continuous} null distribution of the \textbf{test statistic} $t$. The $p$-value ($p$) is itself a random variable such that $\boldsymbol{\color{crukdark}{p \sim \mathrm{Uniform}(0,1)}}$.\par
\endgroup

\vspace{-0.1em}

```{r pvalue-uniform, fig.width=7.6, fig.height=2.4, fig.align="center"}
crukdark  <- "#00007E"
cruklight <- "#009CEE"

## Cached: the (seeded) null p-values are simulated once and stored in
## pvalue-uniform-null.rds; delete that file to re-simulate.
n_sim   <- 1e6
df      <- 8
rds_out <- "pvalue-uniform-null.rds"

if (file.exists(rds_out)) {
  p_null <- readRDS(rds_out)
} else {
  set.seed(7)
  p_null <- 2 * pt(-abs(rt(n_sim, df = df)), df = df)
  saveRDS(p_null, rds_out)
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(3.4, 3.6, 1.6, 1.0), mgp = c(2.0, 0.6, 0))

hist(p_null, breaks = 25, freq = FALSE, col = cruklight, border = "white",
     main = expression(bold("Histogram of ") * bolditalic(p) * bold("-values under H0")), xlab = expression(italic(p) * "-value"), ylab = "Density",
     cex.main = 0.95, cex.lab = 0.9, cex.axis = 0.8)
abline(h = 1, col = crukdark, lwd = 2)

ps  <- sort(p_null)
idx <- round(seq(1, n_sim, length.out = 2000))
plot(ps[idx], idx / n_sim, type = "l", col = crukdark, lwd = 2.2,
     main = expression(bold("Empirical CDF of ") * bolditalic(p) * bold("-values")), xlab = expression(italic(p) * "-value"), ylab = "Cumulative probability",
     cex.main = 0.95, cex.lab = 0.9, cex.axis = 0.8, las = 1)
abline(0, 1, col = cruklight, lwd = 2, lty = 2)
```

\vspace{-1.7em}

\begingroup
Simulated $p$-values under $H_0$ ($\mu_1 = \mu_2$) from a two-sample (pooled) Student $t$-test with $5$ units per group ($10^6$ simulations): the histogram is flat at density $1$ and the empirical cumulative distribution function (CDF) tracks the diagonal $y = x$, confirming $p \sim \mathrm{Uniform}(0,1)$.\par
\endgroup

## Controlling the FDR: Benjamini--Hochberg (BH) {.t}

\vspace{-0.01em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Let $p_{(1)} \le p_{(2)} \le \dots \le p_{(n)}$ be the ordered $p$-values: $(i)$ is the \textbf{rank}\par

\vspace{-0.2em}

```{r bh-gamma-line, fig.width=6.9, fig.height=1.35, fig.align="center", out.width="100%"}
crukdark <- "#00007E"; cruklight <- "#009CEE"; crukpink <- "#FF0087"

par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 100), ylim = c(0, 40), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
     xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")

x0 <- 6; x1 <- 94; yl <- 16              # the p-value line, from 0 to 1
g  <- 33                                 # the threshold gamma
## the rejection region, left of gamma
rect(x0, yl - 7, g, yl + 7, col = adjustcolor(crukpink, 0.10), border = NA)
segments(x0, yl, x1, yl, lwd = 2, col = "grey30")
segments(c(x0, x1), yl - 1.5, c(x0, x1), yl + 1.5, lwd = 2, col = "grey30")
text(c(x0, x1), yl - 5, c("0", "1"), cex = 1.0, col = "grey30")

## the ordered p-values, at irregular positions: p_(1), p_(2), ..., p_(k) below
## gamma, then p_(k+1), p_(k+2), ..., p_(n)
px  <- c(10, 16, 28, 40, 53, 89)
lab <- c(expression(italic(p)[(1)]), expression(italic(p)[(2)]),
         expression(italic(p)[(italic(k))]), expression(italic(p)[(italic(k) + 1)]),
         expression(italic(p)[(italic(k) + 2)]), expression(italic(p)[(italic(n))]))
rej <- px < g
points(px, rep(yl, length(px)), pch = 19, cex = 1.3, col = ifelse(rej, crukpink, crukdark))
text(22, yl, "…", cex = 1.6, col = crukpink)
text(71, yl, "…", cex = 1.6, col = crukdark)
for (i in seq_along(px))
  text(px[i], yl + 5.5, lab[[i]], cex = 1.0, col = if (rej[i]) crukpink else crukdark)

## gamma
segments(g, 4, g, 34, lwd = 2.5, lty = 2, col = cruklight)
text(g, 37, expression(bold(gamma)), cex = 1.5, col = cruklight)
text((x0 + g) / 2, 3.2, "rejected", cex = 0.95, font = 2, col = crukpink)
text((g + x1) / 2, 3.2, "not rejected", cex = 0.95, col = "grey35")
```

\vspace{-0.6em}

\begingroup\centering
All $p$-values below $\gamma$ are \textbf{rejected}\par
\vspace{0.1em}
$\gamma$ is chosen so that the \textbf{estimated} FDR below $\gamma$ is at most $q$ (e.g.\ $q = 0.10$)\par
\endgroup

\vspace{-0.1em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ With $k$ the number of $p$-values below $\gamma$, and $f(\gamma)$ the probability that a \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE} null $p$-value falls below $\gamma$:\par
\vspace{0.15em}
\begingroup\centering
$\displaystyle \mathbb{E}(V) = f(\gamma)\,m_0 \le f(\gamma)\,n \;\; \Longrightarrow \;\; \mathrm{FDR} \approx \frac{f(\gamma)\,n}{k} \;\; \Longrightarrow \;\; \textcolor{crukdark}{\boldsymbol{f(\gamma) \le \frac{k\,q}{n}}}$\par
\endgroup

## Controlling the FDR: Benjamini--Hochberg (BH) {.t}

\vspace{-0.01em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ $\gamma$ is the \textbf{threshold}, and $f(\gamma)$ is the \textbf{probability} that a \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE} null $p$-value falls below $\gamma$\par

\vspace{0.4em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ From the \textbf{distribution of the $p$-value}: under $H_0$ it is Uniform$(0,1)$, so the probability that it falls below $\gamma$ is $\gamma$, whatever $m_0$ is\par

\vspace{0.3em}

\begingroup\centering\Large
Hence\quad $\textcolor{crukdark}{\boldsymbol{f(\gamma) = \gamma}}$\par
\endgroup

\vspace{0.5em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Hence $\gamma$ must satisfy the following inequality:\par

\vspace{0.4em}

\begingroup\centering\Large
$\textcolor{crukdark}{\boldsymbol{\gamma \le \dfrac{k\,q}{n}}}$\par
\endgroup

\vspace{0.3em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textbf{BH} chooses the \textbf{largest} $\gamma$ that satisfies this inequality ($k$ is the number of $p$-values below $\gamma$)\par

\begin{tikzpicture}[remember picture, overlay]
\node[anchor=south west, inner sep=0, text width=341pt, align=left, font=\scriptsize, text=gray] at ([xshift=10.7pt,yshift=12.5pt]current page.south west) {Benjamini, Y. \& Hochberg, Y. \textit{Controlling the false discovery rate: a practical and powerful approach to multiple testing}. J.\ R.\ Stat.\ Soc.\ B \textbf{57}(1), 289--300 (1995).};
\end{tikzpicture}

## Controlling the FDR: Benjamini--Hochberg (BH) {.t}

\vspace{-0.01em}

\begingroup
The \textbf{ordered} $p$-values from $n = 1000$ \textbf{independent} tests against the threshold $i\,q/n$ ($q = 0.10$): BH rejects up to the \textbf{largest} $i$ with $p_{(i)} \le i\,q/n$\par
\endgroup

\vspace{-0.5em}

```{r bh-plot, fig.width=6.8, fig.height=2.6, fig.align="center", out.width="95%"}
crukdark  <- "#00007E"
cruklight <- "#009CEE"
crukpink  <- "#FF0087"

## same simulated data as the Storey slide: 800 true nulls + 200 real effects
set.seed(7)
n_bh  <- 1000
m0_bh <- 800
p_bh  <- c(runif(m0_bh), 2 * pnorm(-abs(rnorm(n_bh - m0_bh, mean = 3))))
q_bh  <- 0.10

ps <- sort(p_bh); ii <- seq_len(n_bh)
k_bh <- max(which(ps <= ii * q_bh / n_bh))      # largest i with p(i) <= i q/n
## stop the axis where the p-values leave the panel, so none is clipped
xmax <- 10 * floor(max(which(ps <= 0.032)) / 10)

par(mar = c(3.0, 4.4, 0.6, 0.8), mgp = c(2.3, 0.6, 0))
plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, xmax), ylim = c(0, 0.032), bty = "n", las = 1,
     xlab = "", ylab = "", cex.axis = 0.95)
mtext(expression("rank " * italic(i) * " of the ordered " * italic(p) * "-values"),
      side = 1, line = 1.9, cex = 1.1)
mtext(expression(italic(p) * "-value"), side = 2, line = 3.0, cex = 1.1)

## the BH threshold: a straight line through the origin with slope alpha/n
abline(0, q_bh / n_bh, col = crukpink, lwd = 2.6)
text(xmax, xmax * q_bh / n_bh + 0.0028,
     expression(italic(i) * italic(q) / italic(n)), col = crukpink, cex = 1.15, font = 2,
     adj = c(1, 0.5), xpd = NA)

## the ordered p-values: rejected ones in dark blue, the rest in grey
sel <- 1:xmax
points(sel, ps[sel], pch = 19, cex = 0.5,
       col = ifelse(sel <= k_bh, crukdark, "grey65"))

## the cut: the LAST point that is still below the line
padj_bh <- sort(p.adjust(p_bh, "BH"))   # BH-adjusted p-values, ordered
segments(k_bh, 0, k_bh, ps[k_bh], col = crukdark, lwd = 1.4, lty = 2)
points(k_bh, ps[k_bh], pch = 21, bg = "white", col = crukdark, lwd = 2, cex = 1.2)

arrows(128, 0.0245, k_bh - 4, ps[k_bh] + 0.0013, length = 0.08,
       lwd = 2, col = crukdark)
text(72, 0.0315, bquote(italic(k) == .(k_bh)),
     col = crukdark, cex = 1.15, adj = c(0, 0.5), xpd = NA)
text(72, 0.0270, bquote("reject ranks 1 to" ~ italic(k)),
     col = crukpink, cex = 1.15, font = 3, adj = c(0, 0.5), xpd = NA)
```


\vspace{-1.5em}

\begingroup\centering\footnotesize
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.0}
\begin{tabular}{cccc}
\hline
rank $i$ & $p_{(i)}$ & $i\,q/n$ & $\tilde{p}_{(i)}$ \\
\hline
$`r k_bh`$ \textbf{(=\,$\boldsymbol{k}$)} & $`r sprintf('%.6f', ps[k_bh])`$ & $`r sprintf('%.6f', k_bh*q_bh/n_bh)`$ & $\boldsymbol{`r sprintf('%.5f', padj_bh[k_bh])`}$ \\
$`r k_bh+1`$ \textbf{(=\,\textit{k+1})} & $`r sprintf('%.6f', ps[k_bh+1])`$ & $`r sprintf('%.6f', (k_bh+1)*q_bh/n_bh)`$ & $`r sprintf('%.5f', padj_bh[k_bh+1])`$ \\
\hline
\end{tabular}\par
\endgroup

\begin{tikzpicture}[remember picture, overlay]
\node[anchor=south, inner sep=0, font=\small\bfseries, text=crukdark] at ([yshift=12pt]current page.south) {The \textbf{BH-adjusted} $p$-value $\boldsymbol{\tilde{p}_{(i)}}$: see the slide \textit{FDR-adjusted $p$-values}};
\end{tikzpicture}

## Controlling the FDR: Benjamini--Hochberg (BH) {.t}

\vspace{-2pt}

\noindent
\begin{tikzpicture}[box/.style={draw=crukdark, line width=1pt, rounded corners=3pt, align=center, inner sep=7pt}]
\node[box, fill=crukdark!6, text width=\dimexpr\linewidth-15pt\relax] (bh) at (0, 0)
  {\textbf{BH} controls the FDR at level $q$ when the $p$-values are \textbf{independent},
   or have a specific \textbf{positive dependence} among the \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE} nulls (PRDS)};
\node[box, text width=0.34\linewidth] (by) at (-3.1, -3.3)
  {\large\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{BY}}\\[3pt] \textbf{no assumption} on the dependence\\[2pt]
   {\footnotesize\color{gray} at the price of power}};
\node[box, text width=0.34\linewidth] (st) at (3.1, -3.3)
  {\large\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{Storey}}\\[3pt] \textbf{more powerful}\\[2pt]
   {\footnotesize\color{gray} needs independence (or only local correlation, with many tests)}};
\draw[->, line width=1.6pt, crukdark] (bh.south -| by.north) -- (by.north)
  node[midway, left, font=\footnotesize, text=gray] {drop the assumption};
\draw[->, line width=1.6pt, crukdark] (bh.south -| st.north) -- (st.north)
  node[midway, right, font=\footnotesize, text=gray] {estimate $\pi_0 = m_0/n$};
\end{tikzpicture}

\begin{tikzpicture}[remember picture, overlay]
\node[anchor=south west, inner sep=0, text width=341pt, align=left, font=\scriptsize, text=gray] at ([xshift=10.7pt,yshift=12.5pt]current page.south west) {Benjamini, Y. \& Yekutieli, D. \textit{The control of the false discovery rate in multiple testing under dependency}. Ann.\ Statist.\ \textbf{29}(4), 1165--1188 (2001).\\ Storey, J.\,D., Taylor, J.\,E. \& Siegmund, D. \textit{Strong control, conservative point estimation and simultaneous conservative consistency of false discovery rates}. J.\ R.\ Stat.\ Soc.\ B \textbf{66}(1), 187--205 (2004).};
\end{tikzpicture}

## Controlling the FDR: Benjamini--Yekutieli (BY) {.t}

\vspace{-0.01em}

\begingroup
BH and BY are the \textbf{same} step-up rule --- order the $p$-values, take the \textbf{largest} $k$ such that\par
\endgroup

\vspace{-5.6pt}

$$p_{(k)} \leq \frac{k\,q}{n\,c(n)} \qquad\qquad
\begin{array}{ll}
\textbf{BH:} & c(n) = 1\\[2pt]
\textbf{BY:} & c(n) = \sum\limits_{j=1}^{n} \dfrac{1}{j} \approx \ln n + 0.577 \text{ (large } n\text{)}
\end{array}$$

\vspace{-1.2pt}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Assumptions}: }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Assumptions}: \textbf{none} on the dependence of the $p$-values\par

\vspace{0.45em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}The price}: }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}The price}: $c(n) > 1$ makes the threshold $c(n)$ times \textbf{stricter at every rank} --- not $c(n)$ times fewer discoveries ($c(100) \approx 5.2$, $c(1000) \approx 7.5$, $c(10^4) \approx 9.8$)\par

\vspace{0.45em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ In our $n = 1000$ example, at $q = 0.10$: BH rejects $152$ hypotheses, BY only $\mathbf{75}$\par

\vspace{0.2em}

\begingroup\centering
\textbf{\large BY is the dependence-robust version of BH}\par\endgroup

## Controlling the FDR: Storey's procedure {.t}

\vspace{-0.01em}

\begingroup
\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ BH is \textbf{calibrated} for the worst case $m_0 = n$: every hypothesis is a \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE} null. Storey instead takes into account the proportion of true nulls $\pi_0 = m_0/n$

\vspace{0.45em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ $\pi_0$ is unknown, but it can be \textbf{estimated from the data}: $\hat{\pi}_0$

\vspace{0.45em}

\setlength{\abovedisplayskip}{4pt}\setlength{\belowdisplayskip}{4pt}\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Apply the \textbf{BH rule} with $q/\hat{\pi}_0$ in place of $q$: take the \textbf{largest} $k$ such that
$$p_{(k)} \leq \frac{k\,q}{n\,\hat{\pi}_0} \qquad \text{and reject the } k \text{ smallest } p\text{-values}$$

\vspace{0.45em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ Since $\hat{\pi}_0 \leq 1$ (it is capped at 1), the threshold is \textbf{at least as large} as BH's: \textbf{more power}, and the more hypotheses are false ($\pi_0 \ll 1$), the larger the gain

\vspace{0.45em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Assumptions}: }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Assumptions}: independence, or only \textbf{local} correlation, and \textbf{many} tests for a reliable $\hat{\pi}_0$\par
\endgroup

\begin{tikzpicture}[remember picture, overlay]
\node[anchor=south, inner sep=0, font=\small\bfseries, text=crukdark] at ([yshift=12pt]current page.south) {How $\boldsymbol{\hat{\pi}_0}$ is estimated: see the slides \textit{Storey's estimate of the FDR}};
\end{tikzpicture}

## Controlling the FDR: which method? {.t}

\vspace{-14pt}

\begingroup\small\noindent
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.25}
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{4.15cm} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{1.6cm} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.95cm}@{}}
\hline
\textbf{Method} & \textbf{Assumptions} & \textbf{Power} & \textbf{Best used for} \\
\hline
\textbf{BH} & Independence or PRDS & Intermediate & Positively correlated tests; few true effects ($\pi_0 \approx 1$); too few tests to estimate $\pi_0$ \\
\textbf{BY} & Any dependence & Lowest & Unknown or negative dependence \\
\textbf{Storey} & Independence or local correlation, plus a reliable $\hat{\pi}_0$ & Highest & Many tests, large fraction of true effects ($\pi_0 \ll 1$) \\
\hline
\end{tabular}\par
\endgroup

\vspace{-0.9em}

\begin{center}
\textbf{All three order the $\boldsymbol{p}$-values and use a step-up threshold: they differ only\\ in the constant \emph{dividing} $\boldsymbol{k\,q/n}$: fixed (BH, BY) or \emph{estimated} (Storey)}
\end{center}

\vspace{-1.5em}

\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.35}
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{14pt}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccc@{}}
\hline
 & \textbf{BH} & \textbf{BY} & \textbf{Storey} \\
\hline
\textbf{Threshold} $\boldsymbol{\gamma \le}$ & $\dfrac{k\,q}{n}$ & $\dfrac{k\,q}{n\,c(n)}$ & $\dfrac{k\,q}{n\,\hat{\pi}_0}$ \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

## Storey's estimate of the FDR {.t}

\vspace{-0.01em}

\begingroup
The same $n = 1000$ \textbf{independent} tests: empirical distribution of the $p$-values, with $\alpha = 0.05$ used as a \textbf{fixed cut-off} and $\lambda = 0.5$ above which $p$-values are taken as \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE} nulls\par
\endgroup

\vspace{-0.6em}

```{r storey-hist, fig.width=6.4, fig.height=2.35, fig.align="center", out.width="92%"}
crukdark  <- "#00007E"
cruklight <- "#009CEE"
crukpink  <- "#FF0087"

## Simulated example: 1000 tests, 800 true nulls and 200 real effects.
## True nulls give Uniform(0,1) p-values; real effects (z shifted by 3)
## give p-values piled up near 0. In practice only the mixture is seen.
set.seed(7)
n_st  <- 1000
m1_st <- 200
m0_st <- n_st - m1_st
p_st  <- c(runif(m0_st), 2 * pnorm(-abs(rnorm(m1_st, mean = 3))))
t_st  <- 0.05

par(mar = c(2.9, 4.2, 0.6, 0.8), mgp = c(1.9, 0.6, 0))
h <- hist(p_st, breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.05), plot = FALSE)
plot(h, freq = TRUE, col = cruklight, border = "white", main = "",
     xlab = expression(italic(p) * "-value"), ylab = expression("Number of " * italic(p) * "-values"),
     cex.lab = 1.15, cex.axis = 0.95, las = 1, xaxt = "n")
axis(1, at = seq(0, 1, 0.1), cex.axis = 0.95)
ymx <- max(h$counts)                      # = R, the first bar

## the significance threshold
abline(v = t_st, col = crukpink, lwd = 2.6)
## the alpha label and the pi0-hat label share one baseline (y_top)
y_top <- ymx * 0.93
text(t_st + 0.012, y_top, expression(alpha == 0.05),
     col = crukpink, cex = 1.15, font = 2, adj = c(0, 0), xpd = NA)

## k = observed rejections (as on the BH slides): the first bar, all p-values <= alpha
R_st <- sum(p_st <= t_st)
arrows(0.085, ymx * 0.74, 0.025, ymx * 0.74, length = 0.07, lwd = 2,
       col = crukdark)
text(0.083, ymx * 0.74, bquote(italic(k) == .(R_st)),
     col = crukdark, pos = 4, cex = 1.15)
text(0.083, ymx * 0.64, "observed rejections",
     col = crukpink, pos = 4, cex = 1.15, font = 3)

## number of p-values above lambda = 0.5, marked with a bracket
W_st <- sum(p_st > 0.5)
hbrace <- function(x0, x1, y, h, ...) {
  xm <- (x0 + x1) / 2; q <- (x1 - x0) * 0.08
  xspline(c(x0, x0 + q, xm - q, xm, xm + q, x1 - q, x1),
          c(y, y + h / 2, y + h / 2, y + h, y + h / 2, y + h / 2, y),
          shape = c(0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0), open = TRUE, ...)
}
hbrace(0.5, 1, ymx * 0.28, ymx * 0.065, border = crukdark, lwd = 2)
text(0.75, ymx * 0.525, bquote(.(W_st) ~ italic(p) * "-values" > lambda ~ "=" ~ 0.5),
     col = crukdark, cex = 1.15)

## second line: "(mostly TRUE nulls)", TRUE in a red box as on earlier slides
lab_cex <- 1.05; y2 <- ymx * 0.385
pieces  <- c("(mostly", " TRUE ", " nulls)")
wd <- strwidth(pieces, cex = lab_cex)
x0 <- 0.75 - sum(wd) / 2
xs <- x0 + c(0, cumsum(wd)[-length(wd)])
ht <- strheight("TRUE", cex = lab_cex)
rect(xs[2] + 0.004, y2 - ht, xs[2] + wd[2] - 0.004, y2 + ht,
     col = "red", border = NA)
text(xs, y2, pieces, adj = c(0, 0.5), cex = lab_cex,
     col = c(crukdark, "black", crukdark))

## arrow up from the count to pi0-hat, the proportion of TRUE nulls
pi0_st <- min(1, W_st / (n_st * 0.5))   # capped at 1
arrows(0.83, ymx * 0.60, 0.83, ymx * 0.775, length = 0.09, lwd = 2,
       col = crukdark)
text(0.97, y_top,
     bquote(hat("\u03C0")[0] == .(W_st) / (.(n_st) %*% (1 - lambda)) ~ "=" ~ .(sprintf("%.3f", pi0_st))),
     col = crukdark, cex = 1.15, adj = c(1, 0), xpd = NA)
text(0.97, ymx * 0.85, "estimated proportion of true null hypotheses",
     col = crukpink, cex = 1.15, font = 3, adj = c(1, 0.5))
```

\vspace{-1.4em}

\begingroup\centering\footnotesize\color{gray}
$\hat{\pi}_0$ is capped at 1: $\hat{\pi}_0 = \min\{1,\; W/(n(1-\lambda))\}$\par
\endgroup

\vspace{-0.4em}

$$\widehat{\mathrm{FDR}}(\alpha) = \frac{\hat{\pi}_0 \times n \times \alpha}{k} = \frac{`r sprintf("%.3f", pi0_st)` \times `r n_st` \times `r t_st`}{`r R_st`} = \textcolor{crukdark}{\mathbf{`r sprintf("%.3f", pi0_st * n_st * t_st / max(R_st, 1))`}}$$

\begin{tikzpicture}[remember picture, overlay]
\node[anchor=south west, inner sep=0, text width=341pt, align=left, font=\scriptsize, text=gray] at ([xshift=10.7pt,yshift=12.5pt]current page.south west) {Storey, J.\,D. \textit{A direct approach to false discovery rates}. J.\ R.\ Stat.\ Soc.\ B \textbf{64}(3), 479--498 (2002).};
\end{tikzpicture}


## Storey's estimate of the FDR {.t}

\vspace{-0.01em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textbf{Storey errs on the safe side}: it counts \textbf{every} $p$-value above $0.5$ as a \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE} null, but a few real effects land there too. So it \textbf{overestimates} how many nulls are \colorbox{red}{\color{black}TRUE}, and its estimated FDR is slightly \textbf{too high}, never too low\par

\vspace{0.8em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textbf{Local correlation}: genes are correlated only within \textbf{small clusters} of a few co-regulated genes, positive \textbf{or} negative, with the clusters unrelated to each other\par

\vspace{0.6em}

\settowidth{\hangindent}{$\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ }\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \textbf{Global correlation must be avoided}: Storey counts the $p$-values of \textbf{this one study}. Small clusters each go their own way and \textbf{average out}, so the count is reliable. But if \textbf{all} the genes move together they are \textbf{one} big cluster: the whole picture shifts from study to study, and the count can be badly wrong --- even when every correlation is \textbf{positive}\par

## FDR-adjusted $p$-values: the $q$-value {.t}

\vspace{-0.01em}

\hangindent=9pt\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Definition}: the \textbf{smallest FDR} at which a test would still be called significant. Note: $q_{(i)}$ is the \textbf{$\boldsymbol{q}$-value of one test}, not the FDR \textbf{level} $q$


\vspace{0.8em}

\hangindent=9pt\hangafter=1 $\textcolor{crukdark}{\bullet}$ \colorbox{cruklight}{\color{white}Calculation of $q$-values}: for the ordered $p$-values $p_{(1)} \leq \dots \leq p_{(n)}$

\vspace{0.3em}

\begingroup\centering
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{2pt}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}ccc@{}}
\hline
\textbf{BH} & \textbf{BY} & \textbf{Storey} \\
\hline
$\displaystyle \frac{n}{j}\,p_{(j)}$ &
$\displaystyle c(n)\,\frac{n}{j}\,p_{(j)}$ &
$\displaystyle \hat{\pi}_0\,\frac{n}{j}\,p_{(j)}$ \\
\hline
\end{tabular}\par
\normalsize
\vspace{0.5em}
\footnotesize Two constraints: a $q$-value can never be above $\boldsymbol{1}$, and a larger $p$-value must never give a smaller $q$-value. Both are met by taking $q_{(i)}$ = the \textbf{smallest} of these values from rank $i$ \textbf{onwards}\par
\vspace{0.15em}
Only the constant in front differs: $1$ (BH), $c(n) = \sum_{j=1}^{n} 1/j$ (BY), $\hat{\pi}_0$ (Storey)\par
\endgroup



\begin{tikzpicture}[remember picture, overlay]
\node[anchor=south west, inner sep=0, text width=341pt, align=left, font=\scriptsize, text=gray] at ([xshift=10.7pt,yshift=12.5pt]current page.south west) {Storey, J.\,D. \textit{The positive false discovery rate: a Bayesian interpretation and the $q$-value}. Ann.\ Statist.\ \textbf{31}(6), 2013--2035 (2003). \quad Storey, J.\,D. \& Tibshirani, R. \textit{Statistical significance for genomewide studies}. Proc.\ Natl.\ Acad.\ Sci.\ USA \textbf{100}(16), 9440--9445 (2003).};
\end{tikzpicture}

## Reading a $q$-value off the plot {.t}

\vspace{-0.01em}

\begingroup
The line from the \textbf{origin} through a point has slope $\boldsymbol{p_{(i)}/i}$. That \textbf{single slope} gives all \textbf{three} $q$-values: multiply it by each method's factor\par
\endgroup

\vspace{-0.9em}

```{r padj-plot, fig.width=6.8, fig.height=2.0, fig.align="center", out.width="86%"}
crukdark  <- "#00007E"
crukpink  <- "#FF0087"

## same simulated data as the previous BH slides
set.seed(7)
n_pa  <- 1000
p_pa  <- c(runif(800), 2 * pnorm(-abs(rnorm(200, mean = 3))))
q_pa  <- 0.10
ps_pa <- sort(p_pa)
k_pa  <- max(which(ps_pa <= seq_len(n_pa) * q_pa / n_pa))
## stop the axis where the p-values leave the panel, so none is clipped
xmax_pa <- 10 * floor(max(which(ps_pa <= 0.032)) / 10)

par(mar = c(2.9, 4.2, 0.5, 0.8), mgp = c(2.2, 0.55, 0))
plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, xmax_pa), ylim = c(0, 0.032), bty = "n", las = 1,
     xlab = "", ylab = "", cex.axis = 0.9, xaxt = "n")
## the default ticks stop at 150: label the end of the axis too
axis(1, at = c(seq(0, xmax_pa - 30, by = 50), xmax_pa), cex.axis = 0.9)
mtext(expression("rank " * italic(i) * " of the ordered " * italic(p) * "-values"),
      side = 1, line = 1.8, cex = 1.0)
mtext(expression(italic(p) * "-value"), side = 2, line = 2.9, cex = 1.0)

sel <- 1:xmax_pa
points(sel, ps_pa[sel], pch = 19, cex = 0.45, col = crukdark)

## the line from the origin through the point of rank 152: its slope is p(152)/152
i_ex <- k_pa
segments(0, 0, i_ex, ps_pa[i_ex], col = crukpink, lwd = 2.4)
points(i_ex, ps_pa[i_ex], pch = 21, bg = "white", col = crukdark, lwd = 2, cex = 1.3)
text(40, 0.0240, bquote(italic(p)[(152)] == .(sprintf("%.5f", ps_pa[i_ex]))),
     col = crukdark, cex = 1.05, font = 2, adj = c(0, 0.5), xpd = NA)
text(40, 0.0180, expression("slope of the line" == italic(p)[(152)] / 152),
     col = crukpink, cex = 1.05, font = 2, adj = c(0, 0.5), xpd = NA)
arrows(96, 0.0240, i_ex - 4, ps_pa[i_ex] + 0.0012, length = 0.07,
       lwd = 1.8, col = crukdark)
```

\vspace{-1.0em}

\begingroup\centering\footnotesize
slope: \quad $\dfrac{p_{(152)}}{152} = \dfrac{0.01488}{152} = \boldsymbol{0.00009792}$\par
\vspace{0.4em}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.0}
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{9pt}
\begin{tabular}{@{}ccc@{}}
\hline
\textbf{BH} & \textbf{BY} & \textbf{Storey} \\
factor $n = 1000$ & factor $n\,c(n) = 7485$ & factor $n\,\hat{\pi}_0 = 796$ \\
$\boldsymbol{q = 0.098}$ & $\boldsymbol{q = 0.733}$ & $\boldsymbol{q = 0.078}$ \\
\hline
\end{tabular}\par
\endgroup

\begin{tikzpicture}[remember picture, overlay]
\node[anchor=south, inner sep=0, font=\small\bfseries, text=crukdark] at ([yshift=12pt]current page.south) {At $q = 0.10$ the same test is \textbf{rejected} by BH and Storey, \textbf{not} by BY};
\end{tikzpicture}

## Simulations and practicals

\vspace{1em}

\textbf{Shiny web applications}

\small\url{https://bioinformatics.cruk.cam.ac.uk/stats/shinystats/}\normalsize
